Simulations were performed using OpenDSS software, which is software that was developed for the analysis of power flow in distribution systems.

articleTitle: Robust control of grid-connected converters under wide grid impedance variation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper investigates the robust current control of grid-connected converters operating under wide grid impedance variation. Digital state feedback control gains are obtained based on linear matrix inequalities that ensure the location of the closed-loop poles inside a circle with radius r, included in the unit circle. To guide in the choice of r, here it is proposed the use of a criterion based on the grid-current tracking errors. The proposed procedure leads to control gains which ensure performance complying with IEEE 1547 Std., which is confirmed by means of experimental results and also by real time domain simulations, in conditions that encompass operation under stiff and weak grid, and also grid voltages distorted by harmonics.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Point Tracking through Magic Square for Photovoltaic Modules Under Partial Shading
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Modules in a photovoltaic arrangement can receive different solar irradiation levels. This phenomenon is known as partial shading and causes power losses, multiple maximum power points in the power-voltage curves and overheating of the modules with lower irradiance levels. This work aims to mitigate these adverse effects using a reconfiguration method on the array based on the puzzle technique of Magic Square. Modelling of the photovoltaic modules was carried out in a MATLAB/Simulink simulation environment. The tested arrays have the total-crosstied configuration as well as configurations meeting Magic Square criterion from the original arrangement. In addition, an adaptive Perturb and Observe Method-based Maximum Power Point Tracking is implemented to verify the differences between a standard and Magic Square array under shading. Comparing to the original configuration The Magic Square has presented better maximum power points and can work with a lower current level depending on the tested shading.

articleTitle: Control of three-phase four-wire SSI DSTATCOM integrated to PV generation system
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Hybrid systems play an important role in standalone power generation mainly due its flexibility and reliability. Integration of different generation sources can require various converter topologies. This paper proposes a control strategy for hybrid hydro-PV generation system employing a three-phase four-wire Split-Source Inverter (SSI). The SSI has the ability to feed ac loads with boost characteristic employing reduced switch count. In addition, the proposed control strategy ensures balanced output ac voltages under unbalanced loads providing the required active and reactive power. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate the good performance of the proposed control strategy under balanced and unbalanced linear loads.

articleTitle: Modeling and Real-Time Simulation of High Impedance Faults for Protection Relay Testing and Methods Validation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This work presents a real-time model of high impedance fault. The model allows full relay validation including different types of ground surface. The model is incorporated into OPAL-RT simulator and implemented in Hypersim software, a comparison with ATPdraw is performed. The model and its theoretical basis are presented; the real-time implementation, its results and the issues are discussed.

articleTitle: Coordinated Volt/Var Control for Distribution System based on Heuristic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents a coordinated Volt/Var control strategy of smart distribution grids where the main objective is to minimize the active power losses (kW/h) of the system. The proposed methodology uses the heuristic algorithm which allows the central and coordinated control between voltage regulators, capacitor banks as well as electronic power devices (solid state transformer and others distributed resource). For validation propose and showing the effectiveness of this method, it was applied to a IEEE test network through an integrated interface between MATLAB and OpenDSS software. Two control structure were tested. In the first one, the network was simulated by applying traditional local control and the second one, the same network was simulated by centralized volt/var control developed. The proposal to compare the two structures is to show the reduction of the electric losses when an appropriate voltage and reactive control is applied. All results achieved the proposed objective, reducing the value of the electrical power losses in 24h period without violation the operation constraints established for the correct system operation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Distributed Energy Resources Impact on Islanding Detection Techniques
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: During an islanding event, the distributed resources may keep the system loads operating without frequency and voltage reference from the main grid. Hence, system stability and some equipment operation can be compromised. Therefore, there are many studies proposing islanding detection techniques that allow fast switching of the distributed resources control mode or its disconnection from the grid. Considering this, the present paper aimed to evaluate the impact of distributed energy resources on three islanding detection techniques: one based on under/overfrequency; another based on the Rate of Change of Frequency (ROCOF); and the last one based on the Rate of Change of Power (ROCOP). Thus, it was firstly simulated fault and islanding events on a modelled microgrid. The technique's accuracy was compared by connecting only a synchronous generator in one scenario and connecting a battery energy storage system and a synchronous generator in another one. Additionally, in the second scenario, the energy storage system output power was changed and it was considered the injection and the absorption of power. Finally, it could be concluded that the energy storage system connection caused some variation on the islanding detection techniques, specially in the one based on under/overfrequency.

articleTitle: Load Identification for Smart Grid Management
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Load disaggregation has been the subject of extensive research in literature. Thanks to the wide availability of microcontrollers and circuit devices for communications, the use of extra hardware for intrusive load identification is not prohibitively expensive. This paper discusses methods for disaggregation, "quasi-intrusive", hybrid, and non intrusive load monitoring. The "quasi-intrusive" is described as a hardware for intrusive load identification using power line communications and an ID-tag from a hardware identification chip. The hardware identification chip allows assigning load profiles to a unique device, independently of the load connection point in the local grid. This identification is similar to the media Access Control (MAC) address used in the MAC Layer on the TCP/IP network Model. The use of this identification module can be replaced or shared with a real internet address, for those loads with internet of things (IoT) capabilities. The hybrid proposal, developed in this work, aims at reducing the computational burden when the on/off status of some loads is known.

articleTitle: Proportional-Resonant Stator Current Controller Applied to SEIG Based Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper deals with the development of a load current sensorless control system applied on a distribution synchronous static compensator (DSTATCOM) for the voltage regulation and load disturbance compensation of self excited induction generator (SEIG) based systems. It is considered a three-phase, three-wire isolated system, composed by an induction generator (IG) driven by a constant speed prime mover, and regulated by a three-phase three-leg DSTATCOM. The SEIG stator currents are controlled directly by a proportional-resonant (PR) current controller, which imposes sinusoidal currents and rejects disturbances at the grid fundamental frequency. Experimental results are presented to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed system.

articleTitle: On Effects of PEVs in Islanded Microgrids Resilience
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The continuous developments toward active distribution systems have been providing the necessary conditions for islanded microgrids operation. In this mode, the islanded regions are expected to sustain the system operation within adequate limits, locally performing several control actions previously assumed by the main grid. Among these controls, the guarantee of generation/demand balance is one of the most critical aspects, which due to the limited amount of generation capacity can lead to massive load shedding. In this perspective, this paper seeks to evaluate the effects of plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs) in the improvement of islanded microgrids resilience. For this, a holistic methodology is proposed to determine whether the implementation of sophisticated controls for the use of PEVs as flexible resources render actual benefit for the islanded network. Simulations are held in the IEEE 34-bus test system considering modifications to represent a microgrid environment. The results indicate that the application of PEVs as flexible resources can significantly enhance microgrids resilience in the mitigation of load shedding.

articleTitle: Improvements on Power Flow Control of Voltage-Source-Based Grid-Supporting Converter by Using Virtual Impedance Concept
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The distributed generation (DG) system insertion based on renewable energy system (RES) in the low-voltage microgrids has demanded efforts for a suitable power flow control strategies. Generally, low-voltage microgrids are resistive with a low X/R ratio which results in active and reactive power coupling. The virtual impedance concept (VIC) can increase the X/R making the microgrid more inductive providing the required power decoupling. Differently, from the methods proposed before, this paper investigates the use of VIC for introducing a virtual resistor becoming the network more resistive and decoupled. Simulation and experimental results obtained from a microgrid laboratory setup operating under different scenarios demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Optimal Power Flow Approach Including Wind and Tidal Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Electrical systems with high penetration of renewable energies are increasingly common. Among these sources, wind energy is the one that has most propagated with the technology in great development and the fact that much of the world population density is located in the coastal where there is strong incidence of winds, favoring the installation of large parks that will not need of long transmission lines for delivery this energy. Power through tidal current streams is a promising source as it presents as one of the advantages the high predictability of energy resources. Power systems analysis tools need to include these technologies as they are a worldwide trend. This paper aims to present a probabilistic modeling to include these sources in the optimal power flow problem. For this, wind farms, tidal currents and hybrids ones were modeled. They were included in the network as a form of power injection to analyze the operational system costs. The methodology was applied in the WSCC test system and had shown that the costs are significantly reduced, and that complementarity among the sources is an important factor for the constancy of the output power of the source.

articleTitle: Active and Reactive Power control in a grid-connected Microgrid with Energy Storage Management
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources coordinated with the use of energy storage systems to provide power for a local grid is the main target for microgrids. Microgrids allow better integration of renewable sources, as well as allow adequate management of the storage elements, which bring improvements in power quality of the electrical systems. This paper presents the simulation results of the operation and control of a microgrid consisting of a photovoltaic generation system with energy storage (batteries) and the load in a distribution system. This work is part of the R&D project (Copel, 2016), whose objective is the development of a control system for the management of energy resources and loads of the consumer in the context of intelligent microgrids, as support to the integration of distributed generation. The management method is based on the construction of an optimal control algorithm and a hierarchical control structure of microgrids.

articleTitle: Performance of a Fault Location Method in the Context of Modern Electric Power Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This work performs tests in a fault location method based on sparse voltage measurements considering modern scenarios of electric power distribution systems, in which a large penetration of distributed generation is expected. These kinds of technologies also could provide data that is currently not available for power distribution utilities and can support the fault location process. The technique used in this paper had a slight modification compared to the original one to enable the use of OpenDSS software for power flow calculation. This software facilitates the use of the fault location technique in practical application scenarios because it is a very robust software and largely used by power distribution utilities.

articleTitle: A Holistic Approach - How to Achieve the State-of-art in Cybersecurity for a Secondary Distribution Automation Energy System Applying the IEC 62443 Standard
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Recent events have shown that critical infrastructure systems such as Secondary Distribution Automation (SDA) networks are in focus on the world scene because it has suffered constant cyber-attacks. This high exposure to cybernetic risks is due to the fact that these systems have a relatively low level of protection maturity. Concern about protecting these systems against attacker actions has been growing as the impacts of such intrusions have serious financial consequences, threaten the loss of intellectual property and generally harm the company's image on the market. In order to address the cybersecurity issue of these critical systems from a holistic point of view, the analysis should be based on an international standard addressing the subject in question: IEC 62443. This standard represents an international agreement on best security practices for Industrial Automation Control Systems (IACS). IEC 62443 takes a broad approach and addresses multiple defense concepts by applying a mechanism known as defense in depth, whose purpose is to stop the attacker's action through multiple layers of protection, defining security levels for each layer. The focus of this work is to apply the IEC 62443 Standard in a standard SDA energy system to test the application of the standard, particularly chapter 3-3, in order to achieve acceptable levels of security in the installations.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of a Electric Power Network Segment of Ijuí using the Pi Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents the mathematical modeling of a power transmission line of a primary distribution network segment of a power distribution company from Ijuí city, RS, using real data. The Pi model was used for the mathematical modeling of the system, and a curve fit to describe the load profile of the modeled segment was also performed. Pi model describes the behavior of a power transmission line considering the resistance, the capacitance, and the inductance of the cable, the voltage, the current, and the load of the power network. Computational simulations of the Pi model were performed in the algebraic and numerical computation software Matlab using the Simulink Simscape tool that enables the modeling of physical systems. Experimental data set was obtained through the installation of power monitoring equipments in the medium voltage network of the power distribution company. Simulations results showed that the Pi model capture the characteristics of this system with accuracy, presenting error lower than 5%.

articleTitle: Modeling and control of the Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter applied to the power management of a battery bank
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The increasing inclusion of Electric Vehicles (EV) in to the Electric Power System (EPS) brings together the idea of using the EV batteries as auxiliary elements to supply the demand for electricity at times of great consumption. In order to perform the energy density management that the battery stores and delivers to the EPS, a bidirectional DC-DC converter capable of matching the energy levels between the input and output buses of the system must be used. The purpose of this article is to use the Dual Active Bridge (DAB), on reduced power scale, with high gain of voltage, to manage the process of charge and discharge batteries and presenting the experimental results of implementation.

articleTitle: Linear Programming Applied to Expansion Planning of Power Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Transmission expansion planning has always been a rather complicated task. The options for power grid improvements are numerous, however the amount available for investments is always limited. In this way, mixed integer linear programming is an assistant tool for making the most financially viable decision. The objective of this paper is present a solution to an optimization problem, developed through a power system simulated on Anarede software that have an expected load increase in the next 10 years and need reinforcement interventions to maintain the electrical parameters in the equipment and in the load buses inside the equipment capacity and regulatory limits. The optimization problem was modeled in mixed integer linear programming, and with the assistance of Optimization software, the minimization of investments for a system expansion consideration was achieved. It was verified that the installing of a transformer in parallel with transformer 4-5 and the construction of 20 MW of distributed generation in bus 8 represents the minimum cost to solve all electric problems that will appear on this grid in the next 10 years.

articleTitle: Method to trace the photovoltaic characteristic curves under partial shading conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The I-V curve is an important parameter, because it has the characteristics of PV panel. It shows compactly that happens in the module due external variations. In this article presents a method to trace the photovoltaic curves under partial shading conditions. Also, it mentions the effects of the bypass diode. Lastly, it makes comparisons between curves of shaded panels and panels with regular irradiance.

articleTitle: Connecting a Cluster of Small Renewable Sources to a Power System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper proposes a mixed-integer nonlinear programming model to define the best integration topology for a given set of renewable energy sources. The approach is based on the classical models of transmission network expansion planning, and defines a network topology for the connection of a set of small plants that minimizes the compromise between the investments in construction and the losses of energy over a given payback period. The methodology selects the best operational voltage levels for the lines, specify the substations and the circuit integration points, connecting the different energy sources. A demonstrative case study illustrates the benefits of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Net Zero Energy Building in Brazil: Potencial Smart Buildings?
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)

authors.preferredName: Rogério Diogne de Souza e Silva

abstract: The electricity distribution system is constantly evolving, with the spread of distributed energy resources, smart grids and the inclusion of competitive markets. With the consumer taking on the role of supplier of surplus energy to the network (prosumer), with the trend of expanded participation through the intelligent buildings that will integrate the distribution system actively. In this scenario, the strong correlation of sustainable buildings and smart buildings is evident in the Brazilian case, which has traditional governmental programs that promote the efficient use of energy as a sustainability strategy, with emphasis on buildings, which must follow the international trend, adopting the Net Zero Energy Buildings. Also noteworthy is the considerable increase in the distributed generation of electric energy, building a favorable scenario for the investment in smart buildings. In order to contribute to the studies in this area, this paper presents the active participation of buildings in the electricity distribution network, involving and correlating the concepts of smart Technologies and distributed energy resources, through the review of publications contextualizing the international trend, as well as data on the Brazilian case.

articleTitle: Simulation of a Slider-Crank Mechanism Driven by a Buoy for Wave Energy Converters Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The generation of electric power from non-conventional sources has been in constant technological growth during the last decades. Among the non-conventional sources, the energy produced by the ocean has drawn the attention of many researchers due to their enormous potential, generating studies around this issue. Currently, there exist various types of mechanisms to absorb the energy of the ocean, the wave energy converter, the tidal energy converters, and others. In this paper, we study a wave energy converter through the utilization of Simulink/MATLAB software. The proposed device is a slider-crank mechanism connected to a spherical buoy. To ensure the continuous generation of energy from the device, under different conditions of the wave, a flywheel is implemented. The obtained results would support the development of a design methodology for the dimensional synthesis of the mechanism that will ensure the application of this technology.

articleTitle: DC-DC Hybrid Switched-Capacitor LLC Resonant Converter: All Switches With VDS = Vin/2
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: A novel isolated DC-DC Hybrid Switched-Capacitor LLC Resonant Converter is proposed in this paper, which is the result of the integration of a switched capacitor ladder cell with the LLC resonant converter operating at high frequency. The topologies feature reduced voltage stress across all the switches to one half of the input voltage, and soft switching for all the switches and diodes of the converter. Theoretical analysis as well as experimental results are presented on a prototype that was constructed and tested in laboratory for 1000 Vdc input, 48 Vdc output, and 90 kHz switching frequency, where the measured maximum efficiency reached 97.27%. The proposed converter is suitable for applications that require high input voltage, galvanic isolation and accuracy in output voltage without the need of control.

articleTitle: Day-ahead Power Flow for Isochronous and Droop-Controlled Islanded Microgrids Considering Generators Operational Constraints
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper proposes a methodology of power flow studies considering both control and operational constraints of Distributed Generation (DG) applied to islanded microgrids (MGs) with a day-ahead horizon. The proposed framework solves, for each hour of the day, an iterative process of power flow calculations allied to voltage and frequency adjustments, in order to satisfy the power/generation balance into the MG and also the DGs control and operational constraints. The day-ahead analysis is made by the use of load and generation pre-specified profiles. The framework was applied to an adapted 33-bus distribution test system, with photovoltaic, biomass and diesel-based DGs, considering the use of primary (droop) and secondary (isochronous) control. The results show that disregarding the DGs operational constraints may lead to mistaken decisions on the microgrid planning, and also that inserting secondary control capacity through a DG to a microgrid may be an achievable option to its islanded operation.

articleTitle: Application of the Ideal Compensation Method in Unbalanced Distribution Network Considering Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is the capacitor allocation in unbalanced power network based on the ideal compensation method for compensation of reactive power and unbalance. The tests are performed for the IEEE 34-bus network with low harmonic distortion of voltage. Harmonic distortions of voltage are caused by the harmonic currents injected by the photovoltaic generators allocated in the network. The capacitor allocation cannot cause harmonic resonance in the power network and cannot exceed the maximum limit of the total harmonic distortion presented in IEEE STD 519-2014. The problem is to minimize the sum of the costs of power losses and capacitors in the three phase four-wire distribution network.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Automatic Generation Control Modes Using ANATEM Software
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: System interconnection is a fundamental practice for the optimum use of resources, increasing system realiability and also reducing operating reserves. It is a common practice to interconnect systems, especially in countries with continental dimensions, such as Brazil. In these systems, there is a need not only to control the frequency, but also the power interchange among control areas that compose it, requiring a secondary level in the load-frequency control denominated Automatic Generation Control (AGC). It has three operating modes, defined according to the Area Control Error (ACE): Tie-Line-Bias (TLB), Flat-Frequency (FF) and Flat-Tie-Line (FTL). This article evaluates these types of control against to the occurrence of a sudden load step in the system. The control modes operate according to their functions, and those systems that operate with TLB mode combinations contemplate the frequency control of this mode, which has the characteristic of sharing this control with the adjacent control areas. Therefore, when appropriately modeled, the controls operate according to their functions, and the strategy adopted must be such that no tendency to instability is introduced into the system.

articleTitle: Design of photovoltaic systems on virtual learning platform
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This article presents the development of a virtual learning platform for the design of solar photovoltaic systems. The work carried out involves the inclusion of mathematical models of solar radiation, photovoltaic panels, regulators, batteries and inverters that are integrated to offer a virtual component operation that intervenes in a system for obtaining electrical energy from the solar source. The virtual environment was implemented using the possibilities offered by a graphic programming environment, to facilitate the learning of the design parameters of solar photovoltaic systems.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Oscillatory Transients Generated by Switching of Capacitor Banks using MPA
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: An Oscillatory Transient (OT) can occur in any part of an Electric Power System (EPS), and its basic characteristics are short duration and considerable variances of the amplitude of the voltage and frequencies involved. Focusing on a medium voltage distribution system, one of the main causes of the OT is the capacitor bank switching, which should be differentiated from other situations that may occur. In this research, we present the diagnostic (identification and extraction of characteristics) of OTs generated by the switching of capacitor banks by applying the Matching Pursuit Algorithm (MPA), that is based on a structured data dictionary. The Golden Search (GS) was used to find the characteristic parameters of the OT. The adopted methodology provided a sensible improvement in the search of the parameters, where the number of iterations was reduced and the estimations were stable. Sensitivity tests of the obtained parameters indicated their relevance for the data dictionary that was used. Based on this approach, it was possible to identify the amplitude (instantaneous value) of the OT as well as its duration. The use of the MPA enables researches with diverse signals, where the concern may be linked to the need to identify the origin of the OT observed on a particular EPS. This analysis, for example, can support areas related to power quality and also protection of electrical power systems.

articleTitle: Grid Support of Small-scale PV Generators with Reactive Power Injection in Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The grid codes are expecting that the small-scale photovoltaic generators (SCPVG) have reactive power capability (RPC) and participate supporting the grid during abnormal events. However, the high integration of SCPVG into distribution systems could change their operation because of the node voltage variation. This paper aims to analyze the impacts of grid voltage support in distribution feeders with high integration of SCPVG. The penetration scenario of 100% of SCPVG with RPC was created on IEEE 13 and 34-Node Distribution Test Feeders and three line-to-ground (3LG) and line-to-ground (LG) faults were applied at the farthest nodes from substations. During faults, the node voltage raised up to 37.08% for the 3LG faults and 36.79% for the LG faults. Moreover, the penetration level of SCPVG decreased to 15.5% during 3LG faults and 71.3% during LG faults due to the disconnection or change of SCPVG operation. The penetration level during faults tends to be lower than before it, and the voltage variation can impact on the SCPVG operation. Additionally, the change of the SCPVG operation may impact on short-circuit level of the feeder.

articleTitle: Residential Consumer Satisfaction Considering Tariff Variation Based on a Fuzzy Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This study presents the fuzzy logic application to evaluate the consumer satisfaction against the variation of the hourly tariff in demand response programs (DR). The DR use a tariff signal or dynamic tariff as a method of optimizing the system, is an important tool, with a wide application. The dynamic tariffs look for minimizes peak demand changing consumer behavior through different tariffs during the day. However, the behavior of the consumer against variable tariffs throughout the day is difficult to model and cannot be treated as a single representation of the price pattern. In this study, will be presented the development of a model using the Fuzzy Logic to better elucidate the characteristics of the human behavior against the variable tariff. The model input variables are the price, demand and freedom of time. As output response has user satisfaction, which represents consumer behavior.

articleTitle: Phase Balancing in Distribution Systems Using Greedy Randomized Adaptive Search Procedure (GRASP)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In distribution networks, the phase unbalancing is one of the major problems for electric utilities, since this can cause heavy loading in neutral and protection functions misoperation (among other disturbances). These problems, however, can be solved through phase balancing which is sorted out efficiently through the mixed nonlinear integer programming. Thus, in this work, the GRASP meta-heuristic, aided by a local search through the VNS algorithm, is formulated to balance a large electrical network and to foster a system planning. For this purpose, strategies of the balancing problem are used to guide the search within the space of solutions and, thus, to find configurations which present a minimum unbalancing phase voltage. The tests were carried out in a three-phase 29-bus network and the results obtained were useful to prove the feasibility of the methodology, by means of the improvement of the operation indexes.

articleTitle: Distribution Network Reconfiguration considering Multiple Objectives - A Strategic Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The distribution network reconfiguration is essentially a multi-criteria problem. This issue is a complex problem, whose solution involves necessarily some expertise and a multi-objective optimization. Besides the technical aspects to be considered in this problem, it is necessary to take into account strategic objectives, to obtain network topologies similar to the company operation proceedings. Thus, it is proposed in this paper a multi-objective approach for solving the distribution network reconfiguration problem, considering strategic objective. In this case, priority consumers are also prioritized in the optimization process. A case study based on real data demonstrates the applicability of this methodology, obtaining results according with the company operation proceedings.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Hosting Capacity of a Real Distribution Feeder with Wind Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper has the goal to verify the Hosting Capacity of a real distribution feeder, calculating the power flow in different predefined scenarios. This work also investigates the network parameters that compose the Hosting Capacity calculation as the limits for the insertion of wind generators of network, aiming to improve the current practice of wind generation penetration assessment for the utilities. In order to perform the study, the OpenDSS software was used in parallel with Matlab software. The results obtained have shown the importance of the definition and choice of criteria and limitations of the electrical network equipment that will compose the calculation of the Hosting Capacity.

articleTitle: A New Set of Steady-State and Transient Features for Power Signature Analysis Based on V-I Trajectory
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Among consumers, there is a growing concern with the monitoring of the consumption of each individual equipment or appliance, rather than the consumption measurement of the whole unit. One way of individualizing the consumption is NonIntrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) based on power signature analysis. The main challenges with NILM approaches are the selection of relevant signature features for load identification (classification). Several approaches have been proposed in the literature using steady-state and transient characteristics. Among these methods, Voltage-Current (V-I) trajectories can be highlighted, mainly in steady-state conditions. In this work, we extend the features extracted from V-I trajectories, including new steady-state and transient features. We compare our approach to two other methods based on V-I trajectories recently presented in literature, using three different machine learning classifiers for load identification and a publicly available dataset as a benchmark (COOLL - Controlled ON-OFF Loads Library). Our results show that the proposed approach presents comparable results to those presented in the literature, achieving more than 99% of load recognition accuracy while significantly reducing the number of features. Most of the new proposed features - including transient-related - were selected in a feature selection procedure, demonstrating their relevance in the load identification and classification.

articleTitle: A review and analysis of technologies applied in PV modules
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The implementation of photovoltaic (PV) systems as an alternative source of energy emerges in the electric sector. In this scenario, the challenge arises to present increasingly efficient solutions for PV conversion. As part of these solutions, several types of technology related to PV modules gain prominence in the scientific milieu and in the market dominated by monocrystalline and polycrystalline silicon technologies. Examples are half-cell, double glass, bifacial, PERC, HIT, amorphous silicon, CdTe (cadmium telluride) and CIGS (copper indium gallium selenide) that have the potential for innovation, however, they need to be studied and compared. In this instance, the purpose of this paper is to study the different types of technologies applied in PV modules, verifying the potential of PV conversion of each technology. To evaluate the potential of the technologies, the PV*SOL software was used, limiting an area for the installation of PV modules and simulating the different types of technologies in the limited area. The system with HIT modules presented the best relationship between generated energy and area. HIT technology still presents a high-cost market, meanwhile this technology is expected to be cost-effective in the coming years.

articleTitle: Heuristic Scheduling Algorithm for Load Shift DSM Strategy in Smart Grids and IoT Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Smart Grids (SG) contribute to the modernization of the current electric grid. Among many features, it includes the demand side management (DSM) strategies which deal with the optimization of the power consumption patterns and the efficient use of energy. These strategies play an important role in both the final cost of energy and the control of the peak to average power ratio (PAPR). This paper reviews the main strategies of DSM and proposes an algorithm for a multi-objective optimization (MOO) DSM problem based on the day-ahead load-shifting strategy of scheduling. A discrete time varying model for the price of energy over a day is considered. A greedy search algorithm with limited complexity is employed in order to perform scheduling on the controllable loads, aiming for the minimization of both the total energy daily cost and the PAPR. The loads considered have different average power values and time-constrained allowable intervals to be powered on. The proposed algorithm can deal with the constraints ensuring that all loads will be scheduled and presenting satisfactory results in terms of cost and PAPR minimization.

articleTitle: Optimal design and operation of a CHP based district heating system including a heat storage and electrode boiler to increase self-consumption
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Energy systems with a high share of renewable energy sources (RES) require a large degree of flexibility due to the inherent volatility of wind and photovoltaic based power generation. Here, cross-sector coupling of the power and district heating system can add such flexibility and increase the self-consumption of RES. To couple these two systems, components such as electric boilers, heat storages and combined heat and power (CHP) systems must be optimally sized. Existing optimization algorithms mostly size the components based on volatile energy prices. In contrast, this paper investigates the sizing based on the reduction of network charges for different degrees of self-consumption in two future RES scenarios. For that, the operating mode of an existing CHP system is changed to "power-led" by introducing a hot water storage and an electrode boiler. The optimization determines the best design of the hot water storage and electrode boiler for a district of a town in Germany. It is shown, that such a system can add flexibility to a micro grid and increase the degree of self-consumption while reducing the network charges and thus being economical up to 60 % of self-consumption.

articleTitle: A Stochastic Programming Model for the Planning of Distribution Systems Considering Renewable Distributed Generation and CO2 Emissions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The presence of renewable distributed generation (DG) in electrical distribution systems (EDSs) has been increased in recent years, bringing technical, economical, and environmental benefits. However, the stochastic nature of renewable DG units increases the complexity of the planning and operation of EDSs. Hence, advanced planning models that take into account the uncertain nature of the renewable DG units, as well as their benefits in reducing emissions, are required. This work proposes a two-stage stochastic programming model for the expansion planning of EDSs that considers the uncertainties associated with the renewable DG units, the demand, and the energy price. The objective function minimizes the net present value of investments and operation costs, as well as the cost of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions. The proposed model was implemented in the AMPL modeling language and solved via the commercial solver CPLEX. Tests with a 24-node system illustrate the efficiency of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Multifunctional PV Converter for Uninterrupted Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Multifunctional converters or hybrid inverters are usually connected to the utility grid and can operate on islanded mode due to their association with batteries. The PV systems are commonly implemented using two stages of power processing. The first stage is a DC-DC converter and the second stage is a DC-AC converter. In multifunctional converters, bidirectional operation is necessary to allow the charge and discharge of the battery banks using a single converter. Therefore, these systems need three power processing stages with coordinated control. Battery banks are commonly applied in uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) in order to supply critical loads. However, in PV systems several modes of operation are possible, including the charge/discharge of the batteries and islanded mode. When supplying critical loads, there is a critical situation, related to the transitions between on-grid and off-grid modes, in this paper, the control of this modes are explored as a means to perform uninterrupted power supply to the loads with fast response. For this, the control schemes of on-grid and off-grid modes are detailed. To corroborate this purpose, hardware-in-the-loop results are presented.

articleTitle: Battery Energy Storage System Allocation in Distribution Systems for Power Loss and Operational Costs Reduction
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The insertion of generators in distribution systems modifies the network's historical passive characteristic, allowing the implementation of new operation modes. However, energy storage systems allocation is required to explore every feature provided by the decentralized generators entirely. In this sense, battery energy storage systems provide greater flexibility in the operation of distribution systems. Nevertheless, the battery's power injection/absorption may cause active power loss increase and voltage profile variation if there is not proper planning of its allocation. In this context, this article proposes two allocation strategies, one aiming at the active power losses and the other at the costs of these losses. Both approaches also include indications of voltage variations and violations of the operational limits. Finally, the energy arbitrage is calculated for every possible battery allocation point to verify the possibility of obtaining economic advantages by buying and selling energy in a dynamic tariff system. The allocation strategies are tested in the widely used 33-bus system with demand and tariff of a real system. The results indicate different but feasible allocations for each approach due to demand and tariff volatility.

articleTitle: Analysis of Distribution System Considering Load Uncertainties: a K-Means Clustering Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of distribution system performance considering load uncertainties. A multi-scenario approach is proposed in order to preserve simultaneity and chronological combination of different loads. K-means clustering algorithm is used to reduce an extensive amount of load profiles data, where a sensitivity analysis of the number of clusters is performed, based on power flow studies. The results were compared considering an annual database and a load duration curve approach, as well as K-means clustering methods, taking into account the accuracy and computational burden points of view. Simulation results shows that the introduced method significantly reduced the computational burden while keeping the accuracy, with a lower number of multi-scenarios when compared to other approaches.

articleTitle: Optimum design of autonomous PV-diesel-battery hybrid systems: case study at Tapajós-Arapiuns extractive reserve in Brazil
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Hybrid energy systems are an attractive alternative for power generation, specially in isolated areas. By connecting diesel generator and battery system to solar-photovoltaic or wind-turbine based generators, several benefits are obtained: higher reliability, energy quality and less oscillations in energy delivery. In this work, a photovoltaic-diesel-battery hybrid system in Tapajós-Arapiuns extractive reserve in Brazil is studied. That hybrid system is formed by a photovoltaic generator, battery system, diesel generator and isolated loads that are variable throughout the year. For that purpose, HOMER software was employed, so load-following and cycle-charging dispatch strategies were analysed with hourly-based data for a typical year. Results showed that load-following dispatch strategy is the best option, leading to energy productions of about 85.6% from the photovoltaic generator and 14.4% from the diesel generator.

articleTitle: An Advanced GIS-based Tool for the Analysis of Future Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The growing integration of distributed energy resources (DER) into distribution networks is increasing the complexity of planning and operational tasks carried out by distribution network operators (DNOs). To achieve this in a timely manner, they need new advanced analysis tools to adequately quantify the impacts and the benefits from potential solutions to be seen in future distribution networks. In this context, this paper presents in detail the architecture and implementation of an advanced geographic information system (GIS)-based planning tool, named OpenGIS, to assess the impacts of DER on distribution networks, and to investigate potential solutions for thermal and/or voltage problems. OpenGIS provides a user-friendly graphical user interface, flexible analysis with detailed results in a GIS environment, and is built through the integration of free-license software packages. A real UK low voltage network with residential photovoltaic (PV) systems is used to demonstrate the different features of the tool.

articleTitle: Distribution System Reliability Assessment Using Sequential Monte Carlo Simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This article describes a simulated model of analysis of the reliability of the distribution system, based on Sequential Monte Carlo simulation. Several reliability indices of typical power systems were analyzed in terms of its expected values, such as SAIDI, SAIFI, ENS, CAIDI, CAIFI. Also a major event day duration analysis according to IEEE Voluntary Standard 1366 was made and discussed. The system used to present the methodology consists of four substations and twenty-four feeders, protective and reconfiguration equipment, such as fuses, reclosers, tie switches, knives and automatic switches and circuit breakers were considered for fault isolation or network reconfiguration. This system covers an area of 237.33 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of a state in southern Brazil with approximately 335 MW load, serving more than 116,000 consumers. A 500 year/scenario simulation was performed to provide the results, considering an hourly step. The results for this system were presented, compared to analytical assessment methodology and discussed in terms of their average values, reliability confidence interval and execution time.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization for Robust Control Tuning Applied to Uninterruptible Power Supplies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper provides as a contribution a procedure for robust state feedback control design that optimizes the weights of a discrete linear quadratic regulator through a particle swarm algorithm. Here, the procedure is applied to the voltage control of an uninterruptible power supply, which is an important system for energy storage in microgrids, providing backup power for critical loads during utility system outages. The proposed procedure is based on the optimization of a practical objective function that encompasses the tracking error and the control signal effort considering uncertain load conditions. The control is designed offline, taking into account implementation delay of digital control signals and multiple resonant controllers. Real time simulations based on hardware-in-the-loop indicate the practical feasibility of the procedure for the application of robust control in power converters. The international standard IEC 62040-3 is used to validate the results.

articleTitle: Sizing and Placing EV Parking Lots: Challenges Ahead in Real Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: According to the 2018 Global EV Outlook, the number of electric vehicles (EVs) is expected to increase to more than 10 million by 2020 and 130 million by 2030. A key challenge in this transition, particularly for large countries such as Brazil, is to ensure that parking lots (PLs) have the adequate capacity to cope with this EV fleet and that they are located in strategic places. This paper discusses the importance of considering traffic-flow, EV charging behavior, and distribution network constraints when sizing and locating EVPLs in real applications. In particular, and since PL operators aim at maximizing the return of their investment, this work analyzes the existing publications to point out the necessity to consider diverse aspects together to achieve solutions that ensure the feasibility of the PL installation and operation.

articleTitle: Strategic Location of EV Fast Charging Stations: The Real Case of Costa Rica
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology to strategically locate EV fast charging stations (FCSs) in large territories (e.g., countrywide scale). The methodology can support planning exercises involving stakeholders of the electricity and transport sectors. It suggests a network of fast chargers that can jump-start the adoption of EVs, procuring lower investments where data for optimization is lacking and the demand for the service is incipient, as in most countries. The methodology considers supplying FCSs in metropolitan areas and ensuring their availability in routes connecting distant places, while reviewing the technical feasibility of the locations. The methodology has been successfully implemented in Costa Rica, as it served as technical input to an Executive Order defining the locations of 34 necessary FCSs across the country, and an additional 13 stations that increase reliability. Due to its simplicity and scalability, the methodology can be used in other countries to define the location of FCSs.

articleTitle: A Survey on Smart Grids: concerns, advances, and trends
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The traditional power grids are facing new changes in their structure, with the advent of the power electronic devices and consequently their use to integrate Distributed Generation (DG) sources (mostly from renewables) at the main supply, the energy storage systems (ESSs) working alongside wind farms and solar plants, the presence of smart meters and network infrastructure, allowing the power grid automation and control. This paper presents a survey on Smart Grids researches, focusing on some hot and important subjects such as security, demand response, and power quality. We discuss the main advances, trends and challenges for implementation of real Smart Grids.

articleTitle: Hardware-In-the-Loop Demonstration of Advanced Control Schemes for Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Thanks to recent advances in computing power, orchestrating the operations of distributed energy resources (DER) and network assets in real-time (i.e., decisions within minutes) using advanced schemes is becoming a plausible concept. To this end, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation can become a powerful technique allowing advanced control schemes to be demonstrated in a realistic environment. However, building a HIL-based platform can be quite challenging as it involves specialized software and hardware from multiple domains. To help researchers carrying out similar studies, this paper presents the architecture and the implementation details of a HIL-based platform used to demonstrate real-time management of active distribution networks. The platform is comprised of a real-time simulator used as a proxy of an actual network and a control room-like environment created using off-the-shelf solutions. An AC Optimal Power Flow-based control scheme to manage DER and network assets is applied to a UK-style test network for demonstration purposes.

articleTitle: Customer-Led Operation of Residential Storage for the Provision of Energy Services
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: As residential battery energy storage (BES) and solar PV systems are becoming increasingly popular, the opportunity arises for these devices to be used in the provision of services, enabling customers to further benefit from their investment. This, however, requires an adequate household-level control strategy to maximize customer benefits considering revenues (provision of energy services), cost (grid imports), and the inherent near real-time changes in demand and generation. This work proposes a time-composite rolling-horizon optimization for the provision of energy services, where a mix of high and low granularity periods are used in a mixed-integer linear optimization problem. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated in a year-long case study considering real smart meter demand, generation as well as pricing data from Victoria, Australia. The results show that while customers experience a small increase in grid imports, the revenues from the provision of energy services lead to an overall net benefit.

articleTitle: Battery Storage Sizing and Location in Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid optimization model based on the metaheuristic Evolutionary Particle Swarm Optimization (EPSO) and Linear Programming for solving the problems of sizing, location and network interface technology selection of battery energy storage system (BESS). The batteries are integrated in a distribution network that has dispersed photovoltaic (PV) generation. Thus, a stochastic scenario generation model is also proposed for creating a database for the PV generation, load and energy prices curves considering historical data. The proposed approach is applied with success to the CIGRE MV benchmark network in the European configuration. Several tests were carried out in order to evaluate the EPSO approach for planning and operate BESS into the modern distribution networks. Experimental results indicate that dispersed solutions to locate the batteries throughout of the network were privileged over concentrated solutions. <; Moreover, the results highlight the properties of the EPSO to obtain a robust convergence behaviour.

articleTitle: Pre-Installation Studies of a BESS in a Real LV Network with High PV Penetration
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The usage of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) in distribution systems has been receiving increasing interest in the power industry for applications such as to improve asset loading indices, increase reliability indices through the provision of backup reserve, among others. This paper presents detailed pre-installation studies to connect a 100 kW/255 kWh BESS into a real residential LV network with high penetration of small-scale rooftop PV systems, in the context of a pilot R&D project being conducted in Brazil. Different control modes and settings and their corresponding impacts on the performance of the BESS to play some expected applications are investigated through Quasi-Static Time Series (QSTS) simulations of this network. The results obtained suggest that, if properly operated, the BESS designed has enough capacity to well-perform both grid-connected and islanded applications.

articleTitle: EV Demand Forecasting Model Based on Travel Survey: a Brazilian Case Study
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Global Electric Vehicle (EV) stock is expanding rapidly. As EV penetration grows, the power demand by EV for charging will increase, indicating a potential reshaping of load profile on the distribution network and likely impacts on the distribution transformers. This study forecasts EV load in a large residential network using specific probabilistic modelling approach. The EV load is estimated using light duty vehicles usage pattern based on a trip travel survey analysis. The trip survey is categorized into trip frequency, trip purpose, distance driven, trip time and duration of travel, which are all treated as distribution of probabilities. In addition to the trip survey analysis, the probabilistic model considers the EV type, model, battery capacity, state of charge, on-board charger level and fuel consumption to forecast energy demand by EV. The performance of the distribution transformers in response to the EV behavior are further investigated from the comparison of the proposed EV demand forecasting model with a generic Poisson model. The results show that, depending on EV penetration level, the distribution transformer can be overload, especially for EV participation higher than 50%.

articleTitle: Living Lab for Electric Mobility in the Public Transportation System of the University of Campinas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The transition towards a sustainable electrified transportation model is becoming a promising reality. Economic, as well as environmental aspects, are speeding up this process. The concept of electric mobility rises up due to socio-environmental, technical and economic problems inherent to the use of vehicle moved by fossil fuels. This paper presents the development of a Living Lab for electric mobility in the public transportation system of the University of Campinas (UNICAMP) considering the integration of a sustainable electric station, wide monitoring, and real-time connectivity to investigate technical, economic, and environmental impacts of the massive insertion of electric buses in urban transport fleets. The data gathered from the wide monitoring will be used as a basis for proposing solutions for users as well as for public and particular managers of transportation infrastructure.

articleTitle: A MISO Nonlinear Model of Photovoltaic Panel Based on System Identification
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The growth in the use of renewable energy sources has made photovoltaic (PV) systems increasingly popular. PV systems are mostly composed of a PV panel to generate dc power and an inverter to convert dc to ac power. Many events may occur on the PV modules, resulting in possible faults and loss of generated power, due to their exposure to environmental conditions. Thus, modeling the PV panel allows to determine the estimation of the output power of the PV system. In this context, this paper presents a nonlinear model based on the black-box modeling of System Identification. In addition, Hammerstein-Wiener (HW) model structure was selected due to its simplicity of representing the nonlinearity of the PV panel. The irradiance and temperature on the PV panel represent the input signals for the proposed model. The current and voltage are measured to calculate the output power, resulting in a Multi Input Single Output (MISO) model. The proposed HW model is compared with the classical Single Diode Model and the results show that the proposed model is more accurate.

articleTitle: PMU-based Controlled System Separation Case Study for the Argentinean High Voltage Interconnection System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to analyze the potential use and effectiveness of a PMU-based controlled system separation scheme for the Argentinean electric system, as a means to prevent blackouts and minimize the effect of severe system disturbances and outages on customers. The implementation of the methodology and the expected benefits are demonstrated through simulation studies based on a real cascading outage that occurred in the system. The results of the study show that a controlled islanding system with the considered characteristics could be effectively implemented to reduce the impact of severe fault events.

articleTitle: A Survey of State-of-the-Art on Microgrids: Application in Real Time Simulation Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In this review paper, CIGRÉ's definition of microgrids was adopted. Their main relevant technologies are discussed (distributed generators, energy storage systems and others). Some points in architecture are also briefly considered. In order to provide the reader with a clear picture, five representative microgrids were selected and described. Finally, the topic of microgrid HIL simulation is addressed. A comprehensive review of the literature was used in this work.

articleTitle: Dealing with Energy-Generation Faults to Improve the Resilience of Microgrids: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In recent years, the Control Systems community has given certain attention to the optimal management and dispatch of (renewable) microgrids, specially in terms of energy generation planning. Nonetheless, modern technological processes are very susceptible to faults, specially due to instrumentation issues, and literature seems to lack works that assess their incipient effects in the performance of modern microgrids. This paper surveys the recent works that indeed investigate how to detect, estimate and deal with faults in such systems from a tertiary level point-of-view. Later, Fault Estimation (and Fault-Tolerant control) design methods for microgrids are discussed: open problems are pointed and (future) research threads are raised.

articleTitle: Use of Distribution Network Topological Fractality and Sunburst Charts in the Online Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The integration of outage records, historical weather information and fault management events are used in a risk-based GIS driven proactive management tool. It enables the operator to visualize the hourly risk prediction by the graphical representation of the feeder section with a color to each corresponding risk level. The addition of daily hours to the set of spatial coordinates is well suited to perform online risk mitigation but also increases the visualization complexity. Outputs from the risk assessment must be simple and very informative to promote fast action by control center operators. The simplification step is to use a fractal network approach, which allows the use the box-counting method and the renormalization process where a distribution network is collapsed to one node. This simple node can aggregate information of the whole network by using a circle diagram in form of sunburst chart for dynamic visualization and navigation. The effectively of the designed visualization tool is evaluated under electricity networks from a real-world distribution system.

articleTitle: Industry 4.0 approach aligned with the challenges of grid-connected photovoltaic systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Technological innovations applied to photovoltaic (PV) energy are important for improving the process of conversion and management of energy, being one of the renewable energies challenges. In this occasion, the phenomenon called Industry 4.0 encourages new concepts and methods of work for several areas integrating automation systems, cyber-physical systems, and the internet, facilitating innovations, such as using smarts grids. Thus, this paper aims to show the challenges for PV systems and brings the union of possible solutions applied in a photovoltaic plant with an approach to Industry 4.0. To do so was analyzed the main challenges for each component and proposed a PV system in software PV*SOL with power optimizers, inverter, and PV modules cleaning system. Subsequently, the proposed system is compared with other scenarios. An analysis was made in different soiling losses in PV modules, i.e., situations without the PV cleaning system, and tested the application of Industry 4.0 elements in conventional systems with and without solar trackers. As a result, the proposed scenario generated more energy than the conventional PV system. In situations, without carrying out cleaning in the PV modules the power generation was lower, even with a better global optimization performance due to the power optimizers that mitigates part of the energy losses. Therefore, Industry 4.0 can provide connectivity, visibility, predictability, and adaptability improving better control over the variables involved in PV systems.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Approach for Power Quality Monitor Allocation with Symmetry in Short-Duration Voltage Variations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In this paper, we present a new approach for solving the problem of power quality monitors optimal allocation, for the monitoring of short-duration voltage variations (SDVVs) caused by a fault condition in a power grid system. The problem is treated in a multiobjective perspective with two optimal criteria: minimization of the number of power quality monitors (PQMs) and maximization of the number of identified faults. Non-identification of an event can occur as a result of symmetry conditions in the network, i.e., in cases where two or more faults generate the same signals in some buses, which leads to ambiguity in the monitoring results. Symmetry increases the complexity of both the problem formulation and solution. The problem is described as a multiobjective discrete optimization problem and is solved by the Algorithm for Bicriteria Discrete Optimization (ABCDO) within reasonable computational time. That approach was tested in power grids of different characteristics and sizes. The results demonstrate the proposed methodology applicability for solving the problem in real-size networks.

articleTitle: Practical Analysis of Teleprotection Schemes based on IEC 61850-90-1 using Real-Time Simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Teleprotection Schemes were developed aiming to improve the performance of transmission line protection, which is achieved through an appropriate choice of them. Through real-time simulation, this paper brings a practical analysis and a comprehensive view of the main aspects related to the commonly applied Teleprotection Schemes, highlighting the minimum requirements established by the Brazilian National System Operator (ONS) and providing an aid in the selection of the scheme to be used. Considering the fact that operation and logic particularities of actual relays can generate better performances, two protective relays of two reputable manufacturers are used in this analysis. Tests are carried out using a conventional Teleprotection Scheme structure and a structure based on the communication mechanisms exposed in IEC 61850-90-1 standard, providing a survey of the benefits and contributing to the incentive for a new version of the standard to cover a standardized way of implementing communication between substations.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis Between Particle Swarm Optimization and Mathematical Programming for Optimal Location of Maintenance Facilities
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of maintenance facilities (depot) location in electric power distribution systems with a focus on strategic planning. Power interruptions can be harmful for both society and distribution companies. Determining the optimal number and sites of depot location to handle power interruptions in the long term can improve the quality of service. Through a good depot location, the distance from depots to work orders (WO) is minimized, operational costs can be minimized and customer interruption duration is reduced, which is a good indicator of the reliability of the system. The problem was solved by a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm and a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model. In addition to the real instance, some synthetic ones were generated to compare both approaches in large-sized scenarios. The computational results show that the two approaches are complementary strategies, being presented the scenarios where each proposal could provide better results.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Assessment of Underground Railway Systems Impact Over Distribution Grids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents a methodological proposal to assess the effects of underground systems’ mobile loads (electric trains) over distribution networks. This proposal, based on Monte Carlo simulation, allows generating random operation scenarios for mass electric transportation systems considering movement, energy consumption, and operating conditions for electric trains. In the same way, contingency events, according to N-1 security criterion on power and traction stations, are considered. This method evaluates probabilistic power flows using probability density functions (PDFs). Moreover, risk indexes are computed to measure the minimum or maximum expected values for equipment loadability and voltage profiles, considering a defined level of confidence. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is tested on the future first Ecuadorian subway system in Quito. <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>

articleTitle: Estimation of Electric Demand from Electric Vehicles Using Spatial Regressions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The acquisition of electric vehicles depends on socioeconomic factors and does not occur homogeneously in the different zones of urban areas for the early years of the electric vehicles penetrations. The concentration of these vehicles can be found by spatial regressions that correlate statically the electric vehicles rate by subarea with the socioeconomic factors of their neighboring regions. Such correlation allows characterizing the influence of the inhabitants in neighboring regions to the purchase of electric vehicles. Therefore, this work aims to show how spatial regressions can provide useful information to determine the load growth by the electric vehicles recharging. To exemplify the information quality, provide from such regression classes, the application of two regressions is performed for a medium-sized city in Brazil in order to determine the best location of charging stations for electric vehicles and the maximum diversified demand in each subarea.

articleTitle: An Infrastructure of Dynamic Tariff Management and Demand Response applied to Smart Grids using Renewable Energy Resources and Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents a proposal for a management infrastructure for dynamic tariffs and demand response to support the consumer in an environment of smart grids, in the presence of renewable energy sources and energy storage systems. The possibility of obtaining daily hourly load curves allows the treatment and elaboration of typical load curves, including seasonal ones, to support the management of the own dynamic tariffs, the simulation, and analysis of networks and the planning and operation of power distribution network. Thus, the implementation of dynamic tariffs with the price in real time can bring important benefits, due to an appropriate choice for consumers. In the advanced metering infrastructure necessary for implementing dynamic tariffs in smart grids, this article discusses aspects of technologies essential for its practical implementation, whereby smart meters, communications infrastructure, measured data management system, local area network and operational gateways must interact for the objectives pursued.

articleTitle: State Feedback Control with Full Disturbance Compensation for an LC filtered Grid-forming Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The control of a grid-forming distributed energy resource unit (DER) requires the control of the voltage at its output filter. This is a fourth order system that can be controlled by state feedback. In this control scheme the rejection of disturbances such as load connections, disconnections, and modeling errors, can be improved by disturbance estimation and compensation. This article discusses the required number of disturbances to be estimated to completely compensate the effect of uncertainties on the voltage response. Experimental results show the superior transient and steady-state performance of the proposed control with full disturbance compensation, regarding its counterpart based on measured disturbance compensation.
