This paper presents a solution to the DG interconnection system by using the VSG approach. Differently, from the solutions proposed before, the virtual inertia of the proposed solution employs a controlled time delay inserted into the active and reactive power control loops. Besides, the paper also presents possible solutions for providing a suitable VSG start-up. Experimental results demonstrated the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Curve Fitting Analysis of Expulsion Fuse Links for Protection Studies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This work purpose is support the protection engineer in the modeling of expulsion fuse links using curve fitting. The proposed approach used the fuse time-current characteristic to achieve the polynomial function that represent the fuse link model. Preferred K fuse was used. The polynomial coefficients were obtained by MATLAB software. The polynomial order that best represents the fuse link was determined employing the cross-validation technique. After selecting the polynomial order, the generated curves were plotted to determine the point of intersection between the curves, that is, the maximum value of the current that maintains the coordination between the fuses. The results were promising. In this way, it is hoped to foment the development of new protection studies for power distribution systems.

articleTitle: Performance and Durability Analysis of Photovoltaic Panels under Different Climatic Conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Analysis of the performance and durability of photovoltaic (PV) panels allows a coherent and assertive planning. In this study the main causes of PV panel's degradation are evaluated, thus presenting a way to obtain its degradation rate (DeR). The DeR was applied to a simulation in the program OpenDSS to verify electrical losses along panel's lifetime. Simulations in different scenarios were run to evaluate the degradation levels in different locations. With these results was possible to predict the durability of some PV modules and to validate them with a reasonable precision degree. The conclusion is that in hot climates with high degradation rates, the PV generation may remain higher along the guarantee period than in locations where degradation rates are lower. Thus, this study provides a substantial assertiveness for investments in PV generation.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization of the GMPPT of Photovoltaic Energy Generation under Different Partial Shadding Conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The performance of a photovoltaic (PV) generation system (PGS) is directly associated with the irradiation incidence over the PV panel and the maximum energy will be delivered only for full panel illumination. However, when the PV panel (or strings of panels) operates under a partial shadowing condition (PSC), only a percentage of the maximum power will be delivered. This power can be even lower without a proper configuration of the conversion system. Therefore, we propose a partile swarm optimization (PSO) of the conversion system which improves the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) and ensures that the maximum power will be delivered despite of the partial shadowing condition.

articleTitle: Analysis of Harmonic and Interharmonic Components by Using an Improved Recursive Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Spectral leakage is a phenomenon that is considered a problem and occurs when Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) is used as a tool to identify harmonic components in a frequency spectrum of electric signals, which contains asynchronous sampling or interharmonic components. It may cause errors in presented results that may affect signal analysis. Therefore, application of a technique or combination of techniques is necessary, in order to better characterize harmonic and interharmonic components and enable extraction of their representative factors. In this context, this research aims at estimating frequencies and amplitudes interharmonic present in a signal. This paper proposes a new approach method, based on Group-harmonic Power Minimizing (GPM) and Recursive Group-harmonic Power Minimizing (RGPM) algorithms. The new proposal establishes an identification threshold and is more accurate when compared to the IEC 61000-4-7 standard, recommended for this kind of problem as it detects not only the 5 Hz minimal spectral resolution, but also frequency components of intermediate location with noise. Results indicate a satisfactory characterization of predominant interharmonic components, with low deviation level, both in range and in associated frequency.

articleTitle: Optimal Distribution Network Reconfiguration with Distributed Generation using a Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents the develop of a computational tool for solve the distribution network reconfiguration problem considering the power losses minimization and distributed generation. The proposed tool satisfies the operational constraints of systems, e.g., voltage limits in nodes and the current capacity of lines. The use of a MINLP and a Genetic Algorithm guarantees convergence to good quality solutions. This is a searching adaptive method - based on natural selection and natural genetic. It improves the solutions in combinatorial problems, in each iteration through their operators (selection, crossover and mutation). 14-Bus, 33-Bus and 69-bus test systems and 880-Bus real system were employed to show the effectiveness and satisfactory results of the proposed tool.

articleTitle: Impact analysis of the BESS insertion in electric grid using real-time simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: With the increase of non-linear loads connected to the electrical grid and the use of renewable sources with intermittent generation, it is necessary to use battery energy storage systems (BESS) to provide solutions for electric power quality, besides contributing with the development and reliability of distributed generation systems. In this work, a three-phase inverter powered by a BESS is controlled in order to mitigate the harmonic components derived from the non-linear loads insertion in the electrical grid, and to inject active power to maintain the energy supply at low-generation periods. The paper presents both simulation and experimental results using the OP5707 real-time simulator from OPAL-RT Technologies, which emulates the entire system under study. Different scenarios are analyzed, demonstrating the system's contribution to the energy quality and to the injection of active power in the electrical grid.

articleTitle: Allocation of Fault Indicators for Adaptive Protection Schemes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The development of innovative protective devices for electrical systems has produced new planning problems, such as the study of the adaptive protection benefits and the efficiency in locating faults. In distribution networks, the careful choice of sites for the allocation of fault indicators and protective devices can increase their benefits in improving the network reliability. The best allocation of these devices can be obtained from the solution of a combinatorial optimization problem, which is the focus of this paper. It proposes a mixed-integer programming mathematical model for the optimal allocation of fault indicators. The solutions allow to improve the identification of temporary faults in a distribution network and to improve of recloser-fuse coordination. Also, a Monte Carlo simulation approach is designed to evaluate the quality of the solutions obtained by the optimization model.

articleTitle: The Effect of Local Inverter Voltage Control in Technical Losses on Low Voltage of a Brazilian Distribution Feeder with Increasing PV Penetration
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The integration of Photovoltaic (PV) systems into Low Voltage (LV) is increasing drastically worldwide. It has become a concern for utilities in high penetration levels due the technical issues lead by this new paradigm. Among benefits and impacts, voltage rise and violation is the prime matter. To mitigate this impact, interconnection standards have been amended to allow the PV inverters to regulate voltage locally. By the other hand, the increasing PV can lead a loss reduction. Thus, in order to investigate the impact of different levels of PV on distribution networks on voltage profile and losses, this paper presents a methodology to assess the effect of local inverter voltage control in network losses and voltage profile. The simulations are carried out through MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) and Open Distribution System Simulator (OpenDSS) by using a Brazilian distribution feeder with 6353 customers in several scenarios analysis. The results indicate the usage of local inverter control techniques is an effective operation to minimize voltage rises and to operate the network within the voltage limits. However, there is an appropriate amount of PV for achieve loss reduction. After certain PV level, the losses can increase significantly.

articleTitle: Application of Battery Energy Storage System in Photovoltaic Power Plants Connected to the Distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: As the level of penetration of intermittent sources in the distribution network increases, the dynamism required to maintain the quality of the energy is proportionally higher as it affects the reliability, protection and operation of energy systems. An analysis of the literature shows that the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) is a solution that has been attracted a lot of attention lately. The present work studies the implementation and the control of a BESS in a photovoltaic solar power plant connected to the electric grid, providing power control and offering reserve of energy in case of contingencies. The study is based on computational modeling and simulation using the Matlab/Simulink software and shows that with the insertion of BESS it is possible to provide a constant power to the network, mitigating the effects of generation fluctuations that are characteristic in photovoltaic generation.

articleTitle: Impact Evaluation in Tap-Change Voltage Regulators within Photovoltaic Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Electricity distribution networks must be carefully evaluated in order to benefit from the insertion of distributed generators. Considering the insertion of photovoltaic systems, the continuous movement of clouds can produce variations of difficult predictability on the voltage levels and the power flow generated. Therefore, it is important to know methods to minimize such impacts, evaluating the iteration between generators and voltage regulators, so that the quality of electricity supply remains within the allowable range. The aim of this work is to investigate the performance of tap-on-load and tap changers (OLTC) using the IEEE 34 bus system. Thus, it was considered the presence of photovoltaic generators in IEEE 34 bus system, with different generation conditions, load characteristics (constant or variable) and actuation adjustment time of the regulating equipment. The use of analyzes known as Quasi-Static Time-Series for the electrical simulations were performed in the Open Distribution System Simulator (OpenDSS) software.

articleTitle: Impacts of an improper change of control from P-Q to f-V of an inverter-based DER still connected to the grid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: When a loss-of-main occurs on the frontier of a microgrid, it is possible to supply the loads by intentional islanding, which improves the continuity. It means a distributed energy resource could maintain voltage and frequency with the appropriate control. If the loss-of-main occurs, the detection and the transition between operation modes must be done as fast as possible to decrease the transient. However, too sensitive methods can cause an incorrect control switch. Thus, this paper analyses the impacts of an improper change of control, from grid connected to the islanded control mode, in a distributed energy resource based in voltage source inverter. It is used the IEEE 34 nodes test feeder modeled in the Alternative Transients Program. The results show that if an improper change of control occurs, the distributed energy resource and grid are very affected.

articleTitle: Fault Location in Transmission Lines Using Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents an application of the most recent fault location methods based on Traveling Waves, on an educational Smart Grid. Data was collected from the Grid using a bench oscilloscope and processed in MATLAB. An algorithm receives the signal and calculates fault distance, based on fault region and peak recognition. Wavelet transform is used to separate relevant Traveling Wave frequencies. Furthermore, use of delays between modes of a Clarke transformed signal are measured to determine the line half in which the fault occurred. Smart Grid data is also compared to ATP simulated experiments to determine advantages and limitations of the Grid usage.

articleTitle: Power Flow Management in Microgrids with Heuristic and Evolutionary Approaches
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In recent years, microgrids and electrical energy generation systems from renewable sources have been widely developed and implemented. This paper regards a model of microgrid connected to the utility grid and aims to manage the power flow in order to maximize the state of charge of the energy storage system and the financial gain from the commercialization of electrical energy. Two power flow control strategies are developed: one based on heuristic decision tree and another on evolutionary algorithm. Both of them allow the maintenance of the state of charge of the batteries near the reference interval and presents different results in terms of profit and average state of charge for different parameters.

articleTitle: Alternative Methodology for Smart Grid Proposals Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In most of the projects developed with the participation of companies providing equipment, services or a combination of both, an important part of the success of the project is the evaluation phase of proposals submitted to a Request for Proposal (RFP) process. This evaluation shall be objective and consider all technical and economic factors that matter when deciding for one or another of the proposals presented. The methodology followed and thus the result of the procedure determines the success of the project implementation that in face of a bad decision may lead to significant losses or project failure. To do this assessment entities, such as the World Bank, encourage the use of a methodology that highlights how the technical and economic factors shall be valued, using coefficients that give more or less weight to technical or to economic aspects depending on the project scope. This paper analyzes the methodologies normally used and presents a method that avoids the use of weights between the technical and the economic evaluated factors, thus providing a more direct and less controversial method in the decision-making process. The presented method is considered relevant for example for taking the best decision in Smart Grid projects that involve diverse equipment, software, communications, etc. and different economic factors that must be considered.

articleTitle: Circuit for Monitoring and Reestablishment of PEM Fuel Cell Voltage Using Controlled Short Circuits
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This work proposes a straightforward method to increase the performance of PEM-type fuel cells (FC) by using the controlled short-circuit technique. This method can be applied either to a set of fuel cells grouped in a stack or individually. An algorithm is used to implement a supervision and an operation that applies periodic short circuits across each cell depending on the individual need of each one. This work discusses simulation, design, software development and construction of an Arduino shield-type module to read individual voltage and then to act on cells that are performing outside the appropriate range through calculation and analyses of the standard deviation. The experimental results were obtained by subjecting a prototype module to a simulator in the ohmic range of the fuel cell. Future work consists of integrating this fuel cell module with an electric energy generator as a way to improve the supervision and actuation algorithm.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of Voltage Control Strategies by Decentralized Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Modern power systems frequently operate near to critical operating limits due to the shut-off of many conventional power plants caused by the integration of renewable energy resources in the grid. In the past, voltage control was mainly provided by conventional power plants not only after failures in the grid, but also in case of sudden changes in the reactive power demand. Regarding the shut-off of these generating units, Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) must provide ancillary services such as voltage control, to guarantee a stable and reliable grid operation in future scenarios. Since most DER are connected to the distribution grid level, they are capable to provide reactive power where it is most needed while also aiding the transmission system. However, different strategies such as constant power factors cosφ can lead to overvoltages in low load hours. Hence, new voltage control strategies are already introduced and analysed by several studies using static investigations. This paper will analyse three different voltage control strategies in dynamic simulations in distribution grids under the consideration of load tap changer. Moreover, innovative voltage control schemes are implemented in dynamic models for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), Photovoltaic (PV) and Combined Heat and Power (CHP) plants.

articleTitle: Non-detection zones of an inverter based DER to islanding events and single-phase openings
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Distributed energy resources connected to distribution systems are vulnerable to islanding events and single-phase open. These two events have in common a circuit opening, and it is possible that single-phase opening events result in variations of frequency and voltage that cause protection actuation. Thus, to evaluate the similarity of islanding and single-phase events, this paper presents the non-detection zone to protection functions during events of single-phase open and three-phase open switch. Moreover, different connections of loads and transformer are considered to identify its influence. The results show that in cases where single-phase opening is considered, usually the number of undetectable points is higher than the cases of three-phase opening, and depending on the setting, the rate of change of frequency function trips to SPO and TPO events and the voltage unbalance function can be used to detect SPO events.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Economic Viability of the White Tariff in Conjunction with the Distributed Generation for Rural Consumers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The consumption of electric energy has increased in recent years. In Brazil there are issues related to the supply of this consumption that are able to reduce the impacts on the environment. Seeking to stimulate the efficient use of energy, the National Electric Energy Agency (ANEEL) established a new tariff modality for low voltage (LV) consumers, the White Tariff. In this perspective, this article presents an economic feasibility study of adherence to the White Tariff for rural consumers considering Distributed Generation (DG) constituted by solar energy and biomass. Hybrid Optimization Model for Electric Renewables software was used as a simulation tool for different load profiles. The results showed that the White Tariff can be more advantageous when used in parallel with the techniques of demand management in which the consumer manages his/her consumption habits at peak times with the off-peak time that has a lower cost of the White Tariff.

articleTitle: Hybrid system for static load models parameters identification and electric power system simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Static load models hold immense applicability in Electric Power Systems (EPS) steady-state analysis. This paper describes the most used static load models - polynomial and exponential - and proposes a hybrid system for parameters identification of the described models and EPS simulation, through an interface between the Python programming language and the OpenDSS EPS simulation software. Providing a theoretical foundation, this work presents the methodology implemented in the system, which employs computational optimisation with the method of least squares and the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm, statistical analysis and EPS simulation. Its results, validated with measured data from various load compositions, acquired in a laboratory, indicate that the system has notable accuracy, precision and a wide application prospect in smart grids.

articleTitle: Control Design for Voltage Support of PV Systems in Distributed Generation by Lithium-Ion Batteries Considering SOC Impact
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Due to the constant evolution of intelligent grids, which are being improved all over the world in the energy sector, more and more renewable energy resources are connected to electrical grids. However, such resources are intermittent by nature. This way, energy storage has been often featured to operate together with such source types, as it guarantees a greater trustability to the systems, concerning energy continuity and dispatchability. Furthermore, energy storage may solve undervoltage problems, for both distribution grid at peak time. For this purpose, this work implemented a constant current charge and discharge control based on SOC (state of charge) to solve such a disturbance.

articleTitle: A Self-Healing Technique for a Smart Distribution Grids with Distributed Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In this paper, a methodology will be presented for the restoration of electric energy using the concepts of self-healing and based on the technique of Analytic Hierchy Process (AHP). The goal of this is minimize eletric losses and the number of consumers affected by a system fault. For this, it was considered the variation of the load throughout the day and the possibility of operation in isolated mode of distributed energy resources (DER) by using panels photovoltaics and energy storage system. The tests for the methodology were performed in the modified IEEE 34-bus system, where it was obtained a reduction of the electrical losses in more the eighty percent. And a reduction of the number of consumers in fault in more of the forty percent.

articleTitle: Development of Wide-Area Control Scheme in Power System Toolbox
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The electric power system generation is currently experiencing remarkable changes, since the increasing shares of interments energy sources. To tackle this issue, we propose the implementation of the smart grid feature and intermittent energy source model in the Power System toolbox. It has been implemented in this paper a remote PSS controller applying remote PMU measurements. To explore the small signal stability analysis and control features available in the proposed platform, the parameter of the PSS and were designed by the HIFOO package aim the system damping. Linear and time simulations are used to demonstrate the system performance of the proposed remote controller in the test system with 53% of wind penetration. The proposed controller shows satisfactory damping performance when the measurement time delay is not greater than 200 ms.

articleTitle: Detection of Open-Circuit Faults in Areas Among Meters in Distribution Systems Using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper approaches a methodology based on the usage of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) to detect open-circuit faults inside areas among meters. Moreover, another neural network is used to detect the phase that defects occurs. The load variations in the system are considered to represent features of a real distribution network. The main purpose of this paper consists in verifying the influence of the number of meters and the type of measurement on the ANNs' performance. The method was tested in IEEE 34 bus test feeder.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy-based Controller for Interconnected Systems voltage regulation through FACTS devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Demand variations in large load centers happen naturally and at any time over the day, which directly affects the voltage profile system busses. In this way, reactive power supports are crucial for this kind of control. The strategies for the control of voltage in the buses are the most diverse and in recent times has seen a great improvement with the development of FACTS devices (Flexible Alternating Current Transmission Systems). This work aims to present a review of the most common strategies for voltage control and at the same time present an approach of a Fuzzy reactive power controller for voltage regulation using a fuzzifier and defuzzifier configuration. The simulation was performed in MATLAB environment with the assistance of the Fuzzy Logic Toolbox. Numerical results were held in the IEEE benchmark system. A quasi-steady power flow with a solution through a scanning method was used to prove the effectiveness of the proposed control approach.

articleTitle: A Timing Comparison of Different FPGA-Accelerated Load Flow Solvers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In this work, we show how an FPGA can be used to implement a load flow solver using different algorithms: Gauss-Seidel (GS) and Newton-Rhapson (NR), and we examine the timing of these algorithms. Since the bus voltages are solved iteratively, the number of iterations for one network topology to the next may be different. Due to this variability in the number of iterations, the total solving time is variable. A solver implemented in an FPGA is much faster and much more predictable in the amount of time it will take for the solving to complete, meaning that execution times for these simulations are far faster than real-time. In this work, 2 different load flow solvers, GS and NR, are compared with a detailed timing breakdown for each algorithm, given a specific network topology. We present the timing details for each part of each algorithm with an accompanying example. For the example network in this paper, the NR solver converges in fewer iterations and completes in a much shorter execution time, even though the time for each iteration is longer.

articleTitle: Transmission Cost Allocation using Nodal Methodology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This study presents a sensitivity analysis of the Transmission System Usage Tariff (TUST) within variations of the electric parameters involved in the tax formulation, applied in Brazil transmission sector. Using the currently software employed by the National Electric Energy Agency (ANEEL), the NODAL, for the TUST quantification values applied to generators and loads. Due to the fact that the electric networks have been modifying with greater dynamism, mainly due to the increasing insertion of intermittent sources of renewable generation and distributed generation, it is necessary to analyze the behavior of the current methodology calculation for the TUST into this new context. In this sense, the work seeks to contribute to this analysis, investigating in a quantitative way, the discrepancies in tariff values, simulating different scenarios in the Nodal software. From the results, inferences can be made in order to identify possible improvements in such methodology.

articleTitle: Analysis of Turn-to-Ground and Turn-to-Turn Stator Faults in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Considering the increasing employment of permanent magnet synchronous machine in wind energy, electric vehicles and aviation, a preventive maintenance program becomes crucial in order to avoid unforeseen interruptions that may compromise the performance of this type of machine. The stator faults are a recurrent cause of these interruptions, mainly the turn-to-ground and turn-to-turn types, which are of difficult detection and caused by partial discharges that can quietly persist up to lead to complete destruction of the insulation. The goal of this work is to analyze different possibilities of occurrence of these two fault types, relating to the position of the failure in the coil and the quantity of faulty turns in the coil, in order to provide data for the development of methods of detection based on current signatures. The operation of the machine equipping a wind generation unit is tested through MatLab/Simulink simulations and the obtained results have shown that the severity of the fault depends on the position of the failure for turn-to-ground and on the quantity of faulty turns for turn-to-turn.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicles Insertion in Power Grids and Impacts on Power Quality: A Conventional and Inductive Charging Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This article compares, in terms of power quality, two different types of electric vehicle charging systems: conventional and inductive. The inductive charging has no physical contact with the electric vehicle, so the electricity reaches the vehicle circuit through an inductive coupling. The results of this study shows, through Simulink/MATLAB® simulation, that the inductive charging injects more voltage and current harmonics than the conventional charging, for three scenarios considered of battery charging.

articleTitle: Optimal Directional Overcurrent Relays Coordination using Directional Bat Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Coordination of directional overcurrent relays is most often made based on manual procedures. However, due to its complexity and time-consuming, these procedures have been formulated as an optimization problem. The aim of this paper is to present a directional Bat Algorithm (dBA) as a potential algorithm for optimal coordination of directional overcurrent relays. The dBA performance was compared to others metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Bat Algorithm (BA) when applied to a nine-bus benchmark test system. The obtained results showed that dBA overcame GA, PSO and BA with less total operating time and faster convergence with similar computational effort.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Analysis in Distribution Systems Using Software ATPDraw
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The purpose of the work is to demonstrate the behavior of the electromagnetic effect in systems subjected to typical situations such as short circuits, capacitor bank energization, transfer of loads and entry of operation of distributed generation system. Initially a theoretical approach of the electric sector is contextualized to the subject, and later the research proceeds in the study of the electromagnetic analysis related to the distribution systems. This analysis is performed from the aid of the ATPDraw software, so that the electrical systems are suitably shaped. The simulation aims at presenting the disturbances of the electromagnetic transient under the distribution system and show, from the results, the veracity of the efficiency in the application.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Modal Features Extraction Through the Variational Mode Decomposition Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents a low-frequency power system modal features extraction method for exploiting the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) method. The features extraction process is focused on a time-frequency analysis of nonlinear and non-stationary signals resulting from a large disturbance. The insight from using VMD is that the technique can accurately achieve signal decomposition in obtaining sub-band signals or modes from power oscillating signals. An optimal and recursive time-frequency formulation yields the modes and their instantaneous modal features such as amplitude, frequency, damping and energy, by applying Hilbert transform. The results demonstrate the applicability of the proposition in a large-scale power system.

articleTitle: Estimation of Electric Vehicles in Dynamic Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The market of electric and hybrid vehicles is still small compared to the market of combustion vehicles. However, this is an ever-expanding market. This paper aims to model the increase in electrical vehicles market in Brazil, which could help the electrical demand forecasting for electricity distribution utilities. The System Dynamics and the Bass Diffusion Model are used to represent the proposed system of the electrical vehicle market, first with a qualitative and then with a quantitative model. Three scenarios are simulated to test and validate it. The results show that the methodology used in this paper is adequate to model the system using different nature parameters, such as behavioral, strategic and economic.

articleTitle: Accuracy Analysis of Sun Position Calculation Algorithms: Ineichen and SPA
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Sun position calculation algorithms are widely used in solar tracker photovoltaic plants and softwares to design photovoltaic projects. The scientific community has several algorithms that compute the sun position, and they vary in accuracy, complexity and validity time. The accuracy analysis of the algorithms is important because the different applications require different levels of accuracy. In applications such as measuring instrument callibration, e.g., it is required high precision algorithms. This work presents a statistical analysis of the accuracy of two sun position algorithms: the algorithm proposed by Ineichen, which is used for PVSyst<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software, and the Solar Position Algorithm, taking into consideration both the standard deviation and the maximum errors, as well as quartiles and quantiles. The algorithm that has the highest accuracy is the SPA, where 99% of the samples have solar vector errors below 0.1187695°.

articleTitle: A Bridgeless Boost Half Bridge DC-DC Converter for Electrical and Hybrid Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The present work is to propose an AC-DC converter as a battery charger for hybrid or electric vehicles based on the Boost Half Bridge (BHB) topology. Such a converter has as its main characteristics Bridgeless, it is a single stage, it has galvanic isolation, it allows to correct the power factor at the input of the converter, to promote zero voltage switching for each of its switches through the asynchronous pulse width modulation (A-PWM), in addition to having a reduced number of semiconductors. Furthermore, all the study and analysis, about the power structure, as well as the loop control and the implemented modulation will be presented in the following topics, in order to explain and prove the operation of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Computational Implementation of Different Anti-Islanding Techniques Based on Frequency Drift for Distributed Generation Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Islanding is a subject of great concern in the Distributed Generation literature since it can lead to equipment losses and electrical accidents for the line workers during a maintenance procedure. The anti-islanding strategies are divided in two big groups: passive and active. The passive strategies preserve the power quality, nevertheless, they present a wide Non-Detection Zone (NDZ). Active methods, in its turn, reduces the NDZ by injecting small degradations into the inverter output parameters. This paper approaches a computational implementation of three different strategies of active anti-islanding based on frequency shift. These methods present reduced NDZ, which is one of the key parameters for measuring their effectiveness. Therefore, is presented the methodology for NDZ determination and THD of the current injected into the grid. For corroborating the presented theory, a PV system of 900Wp was connected to the grid through a VSI inverter, being possible to determine the time required for each method for detecting the islanding.

articleTitle: Increase of Load Frequency Using Mechanically Synchronized Generators in Rotating Opposition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper discusses the possibility of a compact mechanical synchronization for electric generators driven by wind turbines or water flux aiming to increase the electrical frequency of the load voltage. This technique can reduce the rates of mechanical gearboxes or switching rates of electronic power converters. This new alternative besides reducing the ratio of the gear multipliers can even totally eliminate them in distributed generation. To prove this principle, it is proposed the use of two electric machines connected in opposition on a single shaft to add their frequencies in order to approach a resulting frequency compatible with the public network or as close as possible to it. Simulations of the proposed circuits were performed in PSIM software and verified in laboratory tests.

articleTitle: A Daily Load Forecasting Method Based on Data Driven Concept
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of short-term load forecasting, a power load forecasting method based on the data driven concept is proposed in this paper. Before establishing the forecasting model, some pre-processing procedure are applied to the given data. Firstly, k-means clustering method is adopted for the collected massive data. Then, the gray correlation analysis method is used to analyze the relationship between the load data and the load influencing factors which can determine the main influencing factors of the load. The coupling rules are established by the CART decision tree algorithm between the main influencing factors and the category. At last, using the least squares support vector machine method to establish different load forecasting models for different types of load data. Taking the historical data of a district in Guangdong Province as an example. Compared with traditional method, the method proposed in this paper is more accurate.

articleTitle: Model Reference Adaptive Controller Applied to a Wind Power Plant with HVDC Transmission
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Commercial offshore Wind Power Plants (OWPP) started in 1991 and the number of installations increases each year, as well as their distances from the coast. For projects more than 70 km far from the coast, the trend is to use HVDC systems, since, in this way, problems with reactive power losses on the insulated cables are avoided. In these cases, on the offshore converter station, a PWM converter is used to produce three-phase voltages by forming a local grid, and also, to transmit in direct current the energy generated by the OWPP to a onshore converter station. In addition, the wind turbines are connected to this three-phase local grid. This work performs the model reference adaptive control of three-phase voltages of the grid forming converter. A three-phase generation converter, whose current control by MRAC is also demonstrated in this work, is connected to this local grid. Finally, simulation results are presented to validate the theoretical analysis..

articleTitle: Battery Energy Storage Systems: Impact Analysis on Different Loads with Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Projects with Energy Storage Systems (ESS) are being increasingly disseminated worldwide, among some factors of this effervescence can be mentioned the rise of the renewable generation sector, specifically the photovoltaic generation, either distributed or centralized, or even the steady growth of the Electric Vehicle (EV) industry. In Brazil, although the use of these elements is still in the beginning, there is a vast market of micro and mini distributed generation that may facilitate the implementation of ESS in the Brazilian Electric Power System (BEPS). This study provides an impact analysis of the insertion of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) into different consumption classes (residential, commercial and industrial), it is also analyzed the feasibility of the use of BESS for the arbitrage service, in order to verify possible reductions in the invoice, given the constant increase in energy tariff prices. The case studies are carried out using the Homer Grid software for loads of real customers from Santa Maria/Brazil.

articleTitle: Linear Load Flow Formulation for Unbalanced Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In this work, a linear model is presented to determine voltages at the nodes and currents in branches of unbalanced distribution networks. An approximate solution for the load flow is obtained from the solution of a system of linear equations, without the need to apply an iterative process as is done in the conventional nonlinear load flow. Numerical studies are carried out using a modified version of the IEEE 34 node test feeder. For the sake of validation, results obtained with the linear model are compared to the results obtained with a conventional nonlinear load flow using the OpenDSS software. Operational indexes are obtained to compare differences regarding power losses and voltages.

articleTitle: Demand Side Management Potential in Brazil with Focus on Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Due to the expansion in the Brazilian energy matrix of intermittent and non-dispatchable sources, such as wind energy, and a decreasing representation of hydro power plants reservoir, which can allow greater control of energy resources, it is necessary to implement additional tools to assist the control between generation and load, bringing greater reliability to the electric power system. In this context, the Demand Side Management (DSM) becomes an ally, since it is possible to obtain the load control during periods of load peak and variability, being a quickly available resource. This paper presents the motivation for introduction of DSM in Brazil and the worldwide panorama of this program usage, as well as obtaining, through simulations, the operational savings deriving from consumption reduction offers, minimizing the dispatch of thermal power plants with high costs. The operational savings observed in the simulated operating week was of around $ 140 thousand, and could reach even higher values, as the consumer market increases its participation in demand reduction offers, contributing not only to reduction in operating costs, but also to the security of electric power system.

articleTitle: Proposal of an Automation System for Measurment of Short Circuit Impedance and Load Loss in Distribution Transformers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper proposes an automation system for the Medium Voltage Laboratory of the Smart Grid Institute in the Federal University of Santa Maria, focusing on the load loss test. It is explained the relevance of the subject, the standard description of the test, the equipment of the laboratory, the used hardware and software to obtain the voltage and current data and the analysis of the results using values of commercial distribution transformers.

articleTitle: D-SVC Controller Analysis in Active Distribution Systems Operation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This work presents a computational tool for power flow calculation based on the decoupled approach of the Newton-Raphson's method that allows to efficiently evaluate the benefits provided by the D-SVC (Distribution Static Var Compensator) performance in the voltage control in active distribution systems. For evaluating the impact of this device on the operation of distribution systems and the efficiency and robustness of the proposed methodology, simulations showing the positive effects of the D-SVC controllers performance are presented in a feeder acting under different topological configurations and levels of participation of distributed generation. The results presented demonstrate the relevance and effectiveness of the proposed analysis tool in terms of facilitating support analysis to operation and expansion of modern distribution systems.

articleTitle: Scenario Analysis for Sizing of Micro-Plants of Tidal Currents for Isolated Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In recent years the oceanic energy has received special attention mainly due to technological improvement, resulting in increasingly competitive costs. In Brazil, ocean energy appears as a strategic alternative and in the upcoming decades can make a significant contribution to the country's energy matrix. The greatest amplitudes and tidal velocities are found in the north and northeast of the country, making this energy resource an option to be considered in small isolated systems. However, there are few studies that present viable solutions for the use of this extractable potential. The availability of kinetic energy from tidal currents is directly influenced by the lunar cycle, making it necessary, in the case of isolated systems, a storage system to guarantee continuity in the power supply. In this paper is discussed the problem of sizing isolated system based on tidal currents. Considering the generating source variability during the lunar cycle, this paper aims to support the establishment of adequate criteria for sizing of a tidal current micro-plant, considering system installation costs and O&M. Sensitivity analysis studies are also carried out to verify the impact of system cost and capacity factor.

articleTitle: Coordination of Overcurrent Relays Using Graphical Method in Interactive Platform
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In electrical power systems, coordination and selectivity of protection devices are extremely important so that when a disturbance or defect occurs in the system must have a actuation of the protection, isolating the defect from the rest of the system. The objective of this paper is to evaluate the coordination of overcurrent relays using graphical method in an interactive platform, this simulation environment allows the visualization of the various actuation curves used by several relay manufacturers. The graphical method was implemented in Matlab Graphical User Interface (GUI) a graphical programming interface containing curves of several standardizations, being able to adjust the slopes of inverse-time curves and adjustment parameters of the instantaneous and timed overcurrent functions, generating a coordination diagram. Results are presented through test cases show that the proposed methodology is effective in coordination relays problems.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Distributed Generation Micro-dispatch Control
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Global growth of distributed generation, especially photovoltaic, has given rise to new markets and new problems: large injection of power at daily intervals without increasing in the level of consumption. This scenario has already created, in certain places, overvoltage problems, harmonic distortion, etc. In Brazil, the standards regulate the connection of photovoltaic inverters, however, the control is not yet subject to standardization. For this reason, this paper presents a proposal of algorithm for this power injection control in accordance with the solutions of problems such as the lack of standardization in the communication protocol of the inverters. The results of the pilot plant application are also presented.

articleTitle: Uncertainties in Virtual Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This article exposes three uncertain elements essential to the efficient, effective and strategic functioning of a Virtual Power Plant (VPP) contributing to the necessary descriptions and implicit searches. VPP presents great flexibility by integrating energy systems with their various types of sources, where they are generally distributed sets of renewable energies, load fluctuations of demands, and the increasing penetration of dynamically connected and disconnected Electric Vehicles (EVs) on the network. Its reliability becomes a challenging issue due to the uncertainties that are inevitable by the intermittent nature. We propose a discussion and classification about the uncertainties that have received much attention recently and are treated as a decision risk of a system operator of a VPP.

articleTitle: Artificial neuronal network for monitoring of energy consumption by a home device
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a device capable of monitoring the energy consumed by a household device. From this information, a consumption profile is model to detect anomalies of operation, during operation, and to detect electrical faults.The prototype of the device is equipped with a current sensor and a communication module, which sends the data to a web application to record energy consumption. The processing of the information, to predict faults, is carried out in an artificial neuronal network with multi-layer architecture implemented in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Islanding Detection for Distributed Generators Based on Artificial Neural Network and S-transform
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The increasing connection of Distributed Generator (DG) in electrical power systems brings benefits such as redundancy; however, problems like islanding are also present. Passive techniques are the most used for islanding detection because they are inexpensive and easy to implement. Nevertheless, these techniques are rather dependent on the power unbalance between the loads and generation at the time of islanding to detect it properly. With the aim of reducing this problem, techniques based on machine learning have received much attention recently. This work proposes a method for islanding detection based on the frequency spectrum at the terminals of the DG, which is obtained using the S-transform. After that, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is used to identify whether or not the event is an islanding. Using a sampling rate of 64 samples per cycle, the method can be easily implemented in digital relays already present in the system. In conclusion, the proposed method obtained a greater precision than conventional methods, and with a smaller detection time, being around 26 ms.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study for Implementing Smart Community in India: A case study of Panipat Project
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Power Distribution system in India continues to be the weakest link prone to high losses, aging infrastructures and poor reliability indices. "Smart grid" generally makes reference to a class of technology that enables Distribution Company (DISCOM) to use computer-based remote control and automation. This paper provides a detailed case study of smart community pilot project where the DISCOM faced challenges like high AT&C losses, increasing peak demand, aging distribution infrastructures and difficulties in identifying fault location during technical outages. A detailed feasibility study was proposed in 4 selected feeders which included smart grid technologies like smart meters, Head end system, SCADA, load breaking switch, meter data management system, Decision making support software, outage management system etc.

articleTitle: Internal fault analysis of squirrel cage induction machine-based wind turbines
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Due to the increased penetration of the wind power systems in the energy matrix of many countries, there is a need of improving the reliability of such systems in different scenarios, in particular for cases of aggressive faults in the operation of the wind turbine. This work investigates the squirrel cage induction machine-based wind turbine in cases of stator turn-to-turn and turn-to-ground faults. These faults are not simple for detection in practice and modeling and simulation can be a way for knowing some of their effects. Thus, a complete wind turbine system was modeled in the Matlab/Simulink. In addition, some different fault conditions was analyzed. With the model it is possible to have signatures that facilitate future methods of detecting faults.

articleTitle: Financial Impact of the Binomial Tariff in the Investment in Residential Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The development of financial analysis methodologies for the investment return in photovoltaic distributed generation in Brazil is of interest to residential electricity consumers. In this sense, the objective of this study is to evaluate the financial impact of binomial tariff application on investment return in photovoltaic distributed generation for residential consumers, considering the changes proposed in Brazilian electric sector regulation. The paper consists in the comparison of economic indexes using the current residential tariff and tariff models proposed by the electric sector regulatory agency in recent public consultations. The methodology is based on definition of the energy generated by the photovoltaic systems, financial parameters, technical parameters and obtaining economic indexes. The investment attractiveness in photovoltaic solar generation is first calculated with the current tariff model, the second case is based on the Public Consultation n°. 33 of 2017 and the third case is developed considering the Public Consultation n°. 10 of 2018. The methodology proposed and results obtained aim to contribute to the development of a fair legislation for investors and agents in electric sector.

articleTitle: Optimal Dispatch of a Grid-connected Hybrid Microgrid with Ocean and Solar generation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: An optimal dispatch of a grid-connected hybrid microgrid, with solar and ocean generation, and storage system, has been investigated and solved in this paper. The problem has been formulated as a non-linear optimization process with integer and real variables, which is efficiently solved through a problem oriented metaheuristic. It was possible to identify significant savings obtained due to the shifting of the produced energy supply by renewable sources to times when the energy cost is higher. The results showed that the combination of different renewable sources has significant effects on the microgrid economic and operational performance.

articleTitle: Study on Fault Currents Contributed by Distributed Photovoltaic Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: With the increase in the penetration of inverter-based distributed photovoltaic generation in the Brazilian national interconnected system, concerns arise regarding the operation of the inverters in situations of failure, and their direct impacts on the energy distribution systems. This study, through the methodology of short circuit calculation and the application of a test feeder, proposes a discussion about the direct contribution of the inverters in the fault currents.

articleTitle: FCS-MPC Applied to HVAC Control for Demand side Management Purposes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)

authors.preferredName: Júlio Cesar Santana da Rosa Filho
Teresa Irene M. M. de Carvalho

abstract: Users' appliances may be used by a Smart Grid system agent in order to provide services such as voltage regulation (VR), under a Demand Side Management program (DSM). To accomplish that, this work employed a Finite Control Set Model Predictive Controller (FCS-MPC) to control users' Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) units' reactive consumption, in order to make them respond reducing their temperature setpoints when the bus voltage was out of its allowable limits. Computer simulations were carried using a modified version of IEEE 13 node test feeder. A reduction of approximately 29% of reactive power consumption was accomplished during the control actuation, followed by a phase voltage profile improvement.

articleTitle: Analysis of Macroregional Load Curve Patterns in relation to Physical and Socioeconomic Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The human activities dependence on electric energy turns the electric sector to fundamental part of the modern society development. Planning and operation studies are necessary to guarantee the energy supply with safety and quality. All the investments made to cover these studies are charged in the form of tariffs, which includes the energy matrix, required demand, the energy amount used and the consumption time. These last two characteristics defines the system load curve. Thus, the loadshape mapping is the first step to carry out a planning study, in order to determine load variations, patterns and assist in the modeling of other studies, such as load forecasting. Based on this idea, this work presents an analysis of the Brazilian South Subsystem load profile, classified in curves for weekdays, Saturdays and Sundays from 2012 to 2016, aggregating the seasons climates, for the year 2016. In order to compare the curves, behave, a method is developed to determine the hourly variation of the demand. Finally, an evaluation showing the economic and energy relation, comparing the evolution of consumption, within the applied horizon, with the evolution of gross domestic product (GDP).

articleTitle: Main Effects Due to Distributed Energy Resources Connected to Distribution Network of Medium Voltage
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This research project presents different simulations in CYMDIST program, in order to determine the feasibility of a micro-network that would have electrical batteries in the medium voltage network of a Centrosur feeder, which has generation distributed in the Gualaceo town. The purpose is to determine the best connection to reduce energy losses, considering that there is an excess of the generation that could be stored in off-peak hours. The Gualaceo mini hydroelectric plant is chosen since can work independently or be connected to the distribution utility. In addition, an energy storage system will be tested.

articleTitle: DG real-time dispatch order for demand control: a case study with the UFSM microgrid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The use of distributed generation (DG) allied to smart grids offers a series of benefits for the electrical system and, consequently, the society that makes use of it. Specifically, in the economic and planning area, bringing solutions that propose a union between improving the electrical system and reducing operating costs is very interesting. Thus, this article addresses a monthly demand forecasting analysis based on the simple linear regression method, using as tool Open DSS software for the feasibility study and economic advantages of the application of an adaptive control for intelligent dispatch of distributed generation applied to the network Federal University of Santa Maria (UFSM) - case study. As research results, it became possible to structure a programming routine that enabled the insertion of intelligent energy generation, as well as a more accurate verification of the impacts on the load and the economy of the analyzed network.

articleTitle: Design of the Input Capacitance and Inductance in PV Converters
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This work shows a procedure to build a PV one diode model that use only the datasheet data to obtain the I - V curve. This procedure was presented in the literature, but the equations were not clear to obtain the parameters. After a review the revised equations were presented. The simple model was used to estimate the power reduction when pulsed input current or continuous input current converters are used. The ripple produced by these converters reduces the extracted power even if a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control technique is used. For pulsed input current converters, the filter capacitance is needed and if the ripple is not correctly reduced there is a significant power reduction or the MPPT control is unfeasible. The contributions of this paper are providing guidelines, equations and graphs in order to design input components or filters to ensure that the connected converter can achieve its best operation point or the best MPPT control for all conditions.

articleTitle: Statistical evaluation and demand forecasting of emergency service demand in electric power distribution utilities
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In this study, the emergency service order demand is analyzed in the context of an electricity distribution company. The main consequence of considering theses services is the reduction on the capacity planning level previously defined, thus suggesting an estimation in order to promote a better capacity plan. The statistical analysis herein proceed comprises the data separation on the basis of the day of the week, from actual data provided by an electric utility from the south of Brazil. Based on the appropriate distributions for each day of the week, random numbers were generated in order to forecast, for a period of 28 days, the demand demanded for the company’s teams. The results found it has an amplitude of 0.09% and 0.76% for a variability of date based in the real historic series and the forecastings.

articleTitle: DFIG Model Considering Turbine Mechanical Limitations for Frequency Response Control Studies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents a low-order model to study the frequency response capability of DFIG-based wind parks with primary droop and synthetic inertia controls, considering the physical limits of shaft speed, torques and blade pitch angle. The model takes as inputs: the turbine's spinning reserve margin; the wind speed; synthetic inertia constant; droop gain; and the wind penetration. The model can be used by both system operators and agents to: determine the frequency deviation of the power system at different wind penetrations; determine the available synthetic inertia of the wind park; and the effect of the control on the speed and torques of the wind turbines.

articleTitle: Intentional Islanding Case Presentation for a University Campus
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents a proposal for the operation of a Smart Grid in cases of intentional islanding through the rejection of non-priority loads and continuous operation of priority loads in a university campus. This operation occurs through alternative energy sources, such as diesel generator, photovoltaic panels with batteries capable of maintaining the loads operation, and integrated control and protection devices. One-line diagrams of power grid from Campus Palmas of Federal University of Tocantins (UFT) are presented to illustrate the operation of the electrical grid, showing the impacts and technical benefits of the Smart Grid. It is possible to use this study for applications in other university campuses, future studies of economic viability and proposals of technical improvements of operation.

articleTitle: An Proposal to Energy Consumption Estimation of Residential Loads based on State Sensors Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents an approach for household electricity consumption monitoring using state sensors devices (SSD) and electric load models. More specially, the state sensor circuit indicates the load states (On/Off) as well as the appliance (ID) identification number, which are stored in the cloud together with the real load power signatures acquired earlier. Based on the stored information, the proposed method estimates the average consumption per appliance and the total energy consumption. The method is based on ILM (Intrusive Load Monitoring) techniques and is suitable for on/off load types. The approach was tested for the following loads: fridge, air conditioner and microwave oven. The results show that the energy estimation from this method achieves an error lower than 10%, compared with power analyzer measurements. So, this is an interesting option to commercial smart plugs, since SSD is a cost-effective solution and can help users to save energy.

articleTitle: Automation of Manual Switches in Distribution Networks Focused on Self-Healing: A Step toward Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This work describes the self-healing systems and their benefits in the power distribution networks, with the objective of indicating which manual switch should become, as a matter of priority, automatic. The computational tool used is based on graph theory, genetic algorithms and multicriteria evaluation. There are benefits for consumers, that will benefit from a more reliable and stable system, and for the utility, that can reduce costs with team field and financial compensations payed to consumers in case of continuity indexes violation. Data from a real distribution network from the state of Sao Paulo will be used as a case study for the application of the methodology.

articleTitle: Belief Network for Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring Methodology and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper proposes Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) technique using Bayesian networks to identify which load turn-on in certain condition. Explain how to find the values for the conditional probability tables (CPT's) and presents a methodology to implement the network structure. The information used in the inference are defined as Boolean variables, related with well-defined thresholds, to then be used in Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) to infer its probabilities. An interface in LabView was developed to question the system, including the MCMC implementation. The measures and characteristics to identify each specific load are shown, and also the advantages of using changeable thresholds.

articleTitle: Recharging electric vehicles: Impact on the load curve of a low-voltage distribution network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are becoming an option for electrifying urban mobility. Their global sales are growing and their use by ordinary users is becoming more popular. This growth increases the number of EVs that charge using residential power plugs, thereby motivating studies to evaluate the electrical demand generated by these connections. One concern with regard to EVs is how they will affect the components that make up electricity-distribution networks. Regarding smart-grid issues, the penetration of EVs into low-voltage distribution networks is becoming more complex; however, management solutions can be adopted to reduce the impact of their loads on the network. This article presents a methodology to assess the impact of Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs) that recharge their batteries, on the load curve of a low-voltage distribution network. This approach is supported by an algorithm that was developed using the MATLAB® program to determine the state-probabilities curve (charging), based on the Monte Carlo method, and estimate the load curve of consumer units and transformers. The application is demonstrated using part of an actual distributing low-voltage network, which serves twenty-six consuming units and is fed by a 45-kVA transformer.

articleTitle: Smart Grid Tools: IoT device-managed power storage through local consumer demand control
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Controlling the demand of electrical energy by an electronic microcontroller with IoT (Internet of Things) capabilities on local energy storage brings important management tools to the Smart Grid environment. A system that seeks to make the best possible use of the energy stored by intermittent microgeneration and with availability of use by the local power grid creates a great environment to achieve savings with some autonomy. In addition, it allows integrate with the batteries of electric vehicles (EVs). However, the possibilities for concessionaires or energy traders are even greater: they may alleviate overloaded nodes in distribution grids, keep batteries charged during storms that could compromise the energy supply, and balance consumers with different power generation capacities in the network, among others. The present proposition intends to demonstrate one of the possible solutions for the control of energy demand based on a IoT microcontroller managed local accumulation, with parameters shared on a data server.

articleTitle: Fault Indication in Distribution Systems Using an LPWAN Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: In distribution networks, the knowledge of the fault location is a powerful tool for electric utilities. The reduction of the outage period has a direct impact on the fees charged to the company, proportional to the duration of the interruption. Also, it's possible to send a team to provide the necessary maintenance, reducing significantly the costs of the team, like man-hours and fuel. In this case, the use of an LPWAN network, such as LoRaWAN as the communication system utilized for the fault indicators presents as an interesting option due to the long-range verified. In this work, a LoRaWAN network is proposed to use as the communication system in fault indicators.

articleTitle: Current Based Three Phase State Estimator for Distribution Systems with Smart Meters Data
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: A Fast current based state estimator is presented in this paper. The state estimation problem is formulated as three-phase admitting radial and meshed systems. The algorithm has been developed considering several sources of information as input data set, such as power injections, power flows, current injections, line currents, and voltage magnitudes. The applied technique avoids the Jacobian matrix from being iteratively updated improving the speed of convergence, appropriate for distribution systems with a large number of elements. The algorithm is tested on the IEEE-34 bus system presenting good results of convergence and speed, reducing the time up to 2.4 times when compared with a nonconstant Jacobian Matrix, without losing the accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis Of Digital Filters Response By Fasorial Estimation For Protection Of Electrical Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: To ensure that the numerical protection relays act quickly and selectively without compromising accuracy, it is necessary that the voltage and current phasors are free of noise, harmonics and the DC component, and must only contain the desired frequency, thus ensuring that there is no distortion in the reading relay. In this work, the Least Squares Method is used to estimate the DC component that is subtracted from the input signal. The result is processed by the Half Cycle Fourier Filter (HCFF) and the Full Cycle Fourier Filter (FCFF). In order to select the most adequate filter to protect the electrical system, a comparison of the two filters is performed, within and without the step of estimating the DC component before the phasor estimation. In order to make a comparison between the cases and making the choice of the best algorithm, performance indexes are used, such as over-elevation in the output response before the convergence method, maximum error, and convergence time. Finally, it is emphasized that the selection of the most appropriated algorithm should take into account its performance in the index that is most important for its application.

articleTitle: Self-Healing in Distribution Grids Supported by Photovoltaic Dispersed Generation in a Voltage Regulation Perspective
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Distributed Generation Photovoltaic Systems -DGPV - connected to the power distribution grid through electronic inverters can contribute, in an aggregate scenario, to the performance of several power system control functions, notably in self-healing and voltage regulation along a distribution feeder. This paper proposes the use of an optimization method for voltage regulation, focused on reactive power injection control, based on a comprehensive architecture model that coordinates multiple photovoltaic distributed sources to support grid reconfiguration after self-healing action. A sensitivity analysis regarding the performance of voltage regulation, based on a co-simulation of PSCAD and MatLab, shows the effectiveness of using dispersed generation sources to assist grid reconfiguration after disturbances caused by severe faults.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Grid-Connected Microgrids with Different Intermittent Renewable Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents a scheduling model for a microgrid (MG). When a microgrid has an energy storage system, it creates a dynamic system, because the amount of energy charged or discharged at a given time interval affects the future energy stored. The optimization of a dynamic system requires the analysis of its operation over a sequence of time intervals.
