Since a microgrid is subject to some daily cyclic events, such as solar irradiation, wind speed and load consumption, this paper takes into account the microgrid operation, determining when energy should be charged or discharged, when to sell or buy energy from the grid, and the amount of energy involved. The mathematical formulation results in a mixed integer linear programming model (MILP). Three cases are evaluated: MG with wind energy, with solar energy, and the hybrid approach, wind and solar energy together. In all these cases is considered a battery system. Thereby, the MG with wind energy has the advantage to be capable of selling energy when the electricity prices are high and, besides minimizing the purchased energy, the energy sold is maximized.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Perturb and Observe Method with Clustering for Photovoltaic Module with Smart Bypass Diode under Partial Shading
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The photovoltaic maximum power point tracking using perturb and observe method has a fixed step size, where a small step size has a slower time response and more accurate steady-state, while a large step size is the opposite. This work proposes an adaptive step size, proportional to the difference between actual and previous power sample, providing a fast time response and reducing the oscillations at steady-state. The oscillations are smaller with adaptive step size, but they are not annulled and the method presents loss by power oscillations. The clustering is used to eliminate this loss, setting the result of the simple average of the last five voltage samples. The enhanced method has been tested on a 72-cell photovoltaic module with a smart bypass diode per cell under partial shading. Modeling and simulation have been implemented using MATLAB/Simulink. The proposal obtained a faster time response and elimination of oscillations at steady-state.

Author Keywords: Adaptive Perturb and Observe with Clustering

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of Power Distribution Networks with Small Intermittent Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The problem of reconfiguration of electric power distribution networks searches a topology for the network that minimizes technical losses (resistive losses). Finding the optimal configurations is a difficult combinatorial optimization problem that has been gaining a new form over the last decade, arising from the introduction of distributed generation along the networks, and of complementary innovations associated to the concept Smart Grids. A previous paper discussed the characteristics and solution alternatives for the problem in scenarios where there is a small set of random sources with significant energy generation compared to the total energy handled by the distribution network. This paper discusses the problem of unveiling the best network configuration for the operation of a radial distribution network when a large number of small intermittent sources inject energy in the network.

articleTitle: A Simple one-way of Modeling of Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: Although the concept of wireless Power transmission seems recent, this technology is already studied since the end of XIX. The first research to address the topic was from Nikola Tesla. Several works have been developed worldwide with different kind of transmission methods, trying to enable the wireless power transmission in order to amplify the efficiency and transmitted power. One of the methods that shows itself promising and is available in the literature uses the resonant coupling theory. The resonant coupling technology use two identical coils with the same resonant frequency, which increases the coupling of the coils and outweighs the transmission efficiency. In this work was developed a mathematical model to represent the equivalent system of wireless power transmission based on resonant coupling theory using an RLC circuit. The mathematical model was confirmed by measuring, once that mathematical results were similar to the measurement results, and it was observed that the maximum efficiency happens in the resonant frequency of the coils, nearly 1.25MHz. There are other aspects that should be taking into account, like distance between coils, optimization processes and mechanisms to amplify transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: Detection of Appliance Utilization Patterns via Dimensionality Reduction
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: distributed power generation; photovoltaic power systems; power grids; power engineering computing; power generation control; smart power grids; power distribution faults; distribution networks; voltage control; power distribution control.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization and Backward/Forward Sweep Load Flow Analysis for Droop-Regulated Islanded Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency and voltage control implementation for a droop-regulated islanded microgrid through Direct Backward Forward Sweep Load-Flow Method (DBFS) modeled as a particle swarm optimization (PSO) problem. The PSO allied with the Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology of electric vehicles controls the microgrid droop features to improve steady state frequency and voltage. As an advantage, this load flow method runs without the necessity of a slack bus. Simulations are performed in a 33-bus distribution system with distributed generators and electric vehicles, and the results showed the effectiveness and convergence of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Output Structures from Artificial Neural Networks on the Performance of Fault Detection in Power Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: This paper presents and describes a method based on artificial neural networks for single-phase faults detection in power distribution systems. It was evaluated the impact from the number of neurons in the output layer structure and the number of hidden neurons from the networks. The neural networks data inputs are current phasors measured from each phase provided by the allocated PMUs on the distribution system. The testing system used for the simulations is the IEEE 34 Bus. The proposed methodology aims to identify in which phase the single-phase fault occurs ranging from 0 to 20 ohms the fault resistance.

articleTitle: Local volt/VAr Control in Distribution Networks with Photovoltaic Generators
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The Distributed Generation (DG) is characterized by the production of electricity connected to the distribution network or to the local network consumers, using renewable or non-renewable resources, independent of the technology. Excessive use of DG systems connected to the distribution network may cause problems of voltage regulation, compromising the system control and protection devices and the reliability, due to the voltage increase in the DG connection point. In this context, this work presents an analysis of frequency inverters that performs a photovoltaic data transmission interface with an electric grid, as a new possibility of voltage control and reactive power (volt/VAr) in sets with the usual instruments of control used in electricity distribution networks. The analysis consists of performing the volt/VAr control from the frequency inverters in low or medium voltage networks, where the inverter assists in voltage regulation through the insertion and/or absorption of reactive power in the distribution system. In order to demonstrate the proposed methodology application, tests were performed on a standard IEEE 13 node in the OpenDSS® software, comparing the voltage profiles and position adjustment of voltage control for a given DG penetration index and different inverter operating conditions.

articleTitle: Implementable Three-Phase OPF Formulations for MV-LV Distribution Networks: MILP and MIQCP
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference - Latin America (ISGT Latin America)
abstract: The increasing uptake of distributed energy resources (DER) poses significant operational challenges to Distribution Network Operators (DNOs). In this context, AC Optimal Power Flow (OPF)-based approaches have the potential to aid DNOs' decision-making, to enable the operational orchestration of DER and network elements, improving performance while catering for network constraints. However, the classical OPF formulation is non-linear, and consequently, suffers scalability issues when dealing with realistic distribution networks as they can have over thousands of nodes, require three-phase modelling and contain discrete devices. This work extends the authors' previous works by proposing and comparing two implementable OPF formulations (linear and quadratically-constrained) for operational usage in distribution networks considering D-Y transformers. Results using a realistic MV-LV network show that both formulations can successfully orchestrate the operations of DER and network elements. While the linear OPF offers speed advantages when handling discrete variables, the quadratically-constrained OPF has better accuracy with acceptable speeds.
